how-to-get-iec-code.title: How to get an IEC code from DGFT: steps, ₹500 fee, annual update
how-to-get-iec-code.description: Apply for an Importer-Exporter Code on the DGFT portal: who needs it, PAN link, documents, ₹500 fee, timeline and the April–June annual update.
how-to-get-iec-code.h1: How to get an IEC (Importer-Exporter Code) from DGFT
how-to-get-iec-code.answer: An IEC is the 10-character Importer-Exporter Code that DGFT issues against your business PAN. Without it you cannot file a shipping bill or receive export payments through your bank. Apply online at dgft.gov.in, sign with a digital signature or Aadhaar e-sign and pay ₹500. Then confirm or update the IEC online every year between April and June, or it is deactivated.

paras: Any business that exports or imports goods needs an IEC. Customs will not accept a shipping bill without it, and your bank asks for it before it credits export proceeds. The IEC is tied to the PAN of the business: one PAN, one IEC. For a proprietorship that is the owner's PAN; for a partnership, LLP or company it is the entity's own PAN.
bullets: **Manufacturer exporting in its own name:** needs an IEC.
**Factory selling to a merchant exporter in India:** does not need one. The merchant's IEC goes on the shipping bill.
**Service exporters:** need an IEC only if they want to claim Foreign Trade Policy benefits.
**Exempt:** a few categories, such as goods for personal use and certain government and notified bodies.
PAN of the business (the IEC is issued against it).
Address proof of the business premises in the firm's name: electricity bill, rent agreement or sale deed.
A bank account in the firm's name: cancelled cheque or bank certificate.
Mobile number and email you will keep for years; DGFT sends all OTPs and notices there.
A Class 3 digital signature (DSC), or an Aadhaar-linked mobile for Aadhaar e-sign.
For companies, LLPs and partnerships: details of directors or partners.
paras: DGFT now checks many details online against other government and bank records, so some uploads may not be asked for. Keep the scans ready anyway. DGFT can also verify the address physically after the IEC is issued.

sections.h2: Step by step: apply on the DGFT portal
steps: Go to dgft.gov.in and register as an importer/exporter with your mobile number and email (OTP on both).
Log in and open the IEC application (form ANF-2A) under the IEC services menu.
Fill in the business name exactly as on PAN, the address, bank account, directors or partners, and any branch offices.
Upload the documents the portal asks for.
Pay the ₹500 fee online.
Sign the application with your DSC or Aadhaar e-sign and submit.
Download the IEC certificate from the portal and save the login. You will need it every year.

sections.h2: Cost and how long it takes
paras: The government fee is ₹500, paid once. There is no renewal fee, and the annual update is free if you do it between 1 April and 30 June. An agent may charge for filing, but the DGFT fee stays ₹500.

When PAN, bank and address details pass DGFT's online checks, the IEC is usually issued soon after you submit. If something does not match, the application goes to the regional DGFT office and takes longer. Most delays come from a name or address that differs between PAN, GST and the bank.

sections.h2: The annual update: April to June, every year
paras: Under the Foreign Trade Policy 2023, every IEC holder must update or confirm its IEC details online each year between April and June, even if nothing has changed. A no-change confirmation takes a few minutes and costs nothing.

Miss the window and the IEC can be deactivated. A deactivated IEC stops shipping bills at customs and holds up bank remittances. You can still file the update later (DGFT's fee schedule lists ₹200 for an update after the window), and the IEC is reactivated once it is done. Separately, DGFT's rules require you to update the IEC online within 30 days whenever your address, bank account, partners, directors or constitution change.

bullets: Business name on the IEC differs from PAN or GST registration.
Bank account in the owner's personal name for a company or LLP.
Factory address on GST but office address on IEC, with no branch added.
Letting an agent keep the login and DSC. Keep your own credentials.
Forgetting the April–June update, then finding the IEC deactivated during a shipment.
Stopping at the IEC. Next you need the AD code registered at the port, a GST LUT and usually an RCMC.
paras: Next steps: register with your [export promotion council](/guide/rcmc-export-promotion-council), fix your [HS code](/guide/hs-code-for-export) and file a [GST LUT](/guide/gst-on-exports-lut-refund). The [export readiness check](/tools/export-readiness) shows what is still missing, and the full sequence is in [how to export from India](/guide/how-to-export-from-india).
Exportwalla's desk can do this paperwork with you, shipment by shipment, and you review and sign every filing; see [pricing](/pricing) or [talk to us](/contact).

faqs: Is the IEC number the same as my PAN?

Yes. Since July 2017 DGFT has used the PAN of the business as its IEC, and only one IEC can exist against one PAN. A proprietor's IEC is the owner's PAN; a company or LLP uses its own PAN. If you open a new company, it needs its own IEC.
Does an IEC expire?
No. It has no expiry date and no renewal fee. But you must update or confirm it online every year between April and June. If you skip this, DGFT can deactivate the IEC until you complete the update.
Can I apply without a digital signature?
Yes. The DGFT portal accepts Aadhaar-based e-sign as well as a Class 3 digital signature. For e-sign, the Aadhaar of the person signing must be linked to a mobile number that receives the OTP.
I only sell to an exporter in India. Do I need an IEC?

No. If the merchant exporter buys from you in India and exports in its own name, its IEC goes on the shipping bill. You need your own IEC only when you export in your own name, which also lets you claim incentives and refunds directly.
My IEC was deactivated. What now?

Log in to the DGFT portal and complete the pending annual update. DGFT's fee schedule lists ₹200 for an update filed after the April–June window. Once it is submitted, the IEC is reactivated and customs and banks can use it again.
sources: DGFT Public Notice 02/2025-26: Appendix 2K fees (IEC ₹500; annual update nil in April–June, ₹200 after)
DGFT: Foreign Trade Policy 2023, chapter 2 (para 2.05, IEC)
DGFT: Handbook of Procedures, chapter 2 (IEC application and modification)

bullets: **Apne naam se export karne wali factory:** IEC chahiye.
**India mein merchant exporter ko maal bechne wali factory:** zaroorat nahi, shipping bill par merchant ka IEC lagta hai.
**Service exporter:** sirf tab, jab Foreign Trade Policy ke benefits lene hon.
**Chhoot:** personal use ka maal aur kuch sarkari ya notified bodies.
Business ka PAN.
Firm ke naam par address proof: bijli bill, rent agreement ya sale deed.

Jab PAN, bank aur address online checks mein match ho jaate hain, IEC aam taur par submit ke kuch hi samay baad mil jata hai. Mismatch ho to application regional DGFT office jaati hai aur zyada samay lagta hai.

sections.h2: Annual update: har saal April se June
paras: Foreign Trade Policy 2023 ke hisaab se har IEC holder ko har saal April–June mein IEC online update ya confirm karna hai, chahe kuch na badla ho. Yeh free hai aur kuch minute lagte hain.

Window chhoot gayi to IEC deactivate ho sakta hai, jisse customs par shipping bill aur bank remittance ruk jaate hain. Baad mein update karne par DGFT ki fee list mein ₹200 hai, aur update hote hi IEC phir active ho jata hai. Address, bank account, partners ya directors badlein to 30 din ke andar IEC online update karna bhi zaroori hai.

bullets: IEC par naam PAN ya GST se alag.
Company ka bank account owner ke personal naam par.
GST par factory ka address, IEC par office ka, branch add nahi kiya.
Login aur DSC agent ke paas chhod dena.
April–June update bhool jaana.

faqs: Kya IEC number aur PAN ek hi hai?
Haan. July 2017 se DGFT business ke PAN ko hi IEC maanta hai aur ek PAN par sirf ek IEC ho sakta hai. Nayi company banayi to uska alag IEC lagega.
Kya IEC expire hota hai?
Nahi, koi expiry ya renewal fees nahi. Par har saal April–June mein online update ya confirm karna zaroori hai, warna DGFT IEC deactivate kar sakta hai.
Digital signature nahi hai to?
Koi baat nahi. DGFT portal Class 3 DSC ke alawa Aadhaar e-sign bhi leta hai. Bas sign karne wale ka Aadhaar us mobile se juda hona chahiye jis par OTP aayega.
Main sirf India mein exporter ko maal bechta hoon. IEC chahiye?
Nahi. Agar merchant exporter apne naam se export karta hai to shipping bill par uska IEC lagega. Apne naam se export karna ho aur incentives seedhe lene hon tab apna IEC chahiye.
IEC deactivate ho gaya, ab kya karein?
DGFT portal par login karke pending annual update poora karein. Window ke baad update ki fees DGFT list mein ₹200 hai. Update submit hote hi IEC phir active ho jata hai.

rcmc-export-promotion-council.title: RCMC for exporters: which council, how to apply, what it unlocks
rcmc-export-promotion-council.description: Which export promotion council or board issues your RCMC (CLE, AEPC, EPCH, APEDA, Spices Board, MPEDA), how to apply on DGFT e-RCMC and validity.
rcmc-export-promotion-council.h1: RCMC: register with the right export promotion council
rcmc-export-promotion-council.answer: An RCMC (Registration-cum-Membership Certificate) shows you are a registered member of the export promotion council or commodity board for your product, such as CLE for leather, AEPC for garments or APEDA for rice. Apply on DGFT's e-RCMC service using your IEC. It is normally valid for five years and is needed for most Foreign Trade Policy benefits and for joining council fairs and buyer meets.

sections.h2: What an RCMC is and why you need it
paras: Each product family in India has an export promotion council (EPC) or commodity board. The list is in Appendix 2T of the Foreign Trade Policy. When you join the council for your main product, it issues an RCMC. DGFT and other agencies treat that certificate as proof that you are a registered exporter of that product.
bullets: **Foreign Trade Policy benefits:** authorisations and benefits such as Advance Authorisation and EPCG ask for an RCMC.

**Fairs and buyer meets:** councils run India pavilions, buyer-seller meets and delegations, often with government Market Access Support (MAS) under the Export Promotion Mission, which replaced the old Market Access Initiative (MAI).
**Buyer enquiries and market data:** councils pass on enquiries and circulars to members.
**Compulsory for some products:** APEDA products, spices (Spices Board) and marine products (MPEDA) need registration before you export at all.

head: Your product
Council or board
Typical clusters
rows: Leather footwear, bags, gloves, finished leather
Cotton yarn, fabric, bed linen, towels
Handicrafts, art metalware, wooden and decor items
Rice, processed food, fruit, vegetables, meat
Shrimp, fish and other marine products
Many unrelated products, or none of the above

paras: Register with the council for the product that makes most of your exports; your town does not decide it, and the clusters above are only examples. You can hold more than one RCMC if you export in different product families.

sections.h2: How to apply on DGFT e-RCMC
steps: Get your [IEC](/guide/how-to-get-iec-code) first. The RCMC is issued against it.
Log in to the DGFT portal with your IEC-linked account and open e-RCMC, then apply for a new RCMC.
Choose the registering authority (council or board), your products and whether you are a manufacturer or merchant exporter.
Fill in the details and upload what the council asks for: GST registration, manufacturing proof such as Udyam, factory licence or FSSAI, and bank details.
Pay the council's fee online. Each council sets its own fee and some also charge an annual membership subscription.
Sign with DSC or Aadhaar e-sign and submit. The council reviews it and issues an e-RCMC that you download from the portal.
paras: Renewals and amendments go through the same e-RCMC service. Most delays come from missing manufacturing proof or a name and address that do not match the IEC.

An RCMC is normally valid for five years. The period counts from 1 April of the licensing year in which it was issued and ends on 31 March five years later, unless the council specifies otherwise. Renew it online before it lapses, especially before you apply for an authorisation or book a council fair.

Councils may ask members for annual export returns and the yearly subscription. If your name, address, ownership or constitution changes, tell the council within one month, and update the RCMC when your products or exporter status change.

sections.h2: APEDA, Spices Board and MPEDA: registration is compulsory
bullets: **APEDA:** exporters of APEDA-listed products (rice, processed food, fresh produce, meat, dairy, honey and more) must register. APEDA issues its RCMC through the DGFT portal; the fee is ₹5,000 plus 18% GST (₹5,900) and validity is five years. Rice exporters also deal with APEDA's contract registration; see the [rice guide](/guide/how-to-export-rice-from-india).

**Spices Board:** you cannot export spices without a CRES (Certificate of Registration as Exporter of Spices). It is issued for a three-year block, the fee differs for merchant and manufacturer exporters, and renewals are filed through the DGFT portal. See the [spices guide](/guide/how-to-export-spices-from-india).

**MPEDA:** exporters of marine products must register with MPEDA. Processing plants that ship to the EU and several other markets also need approval through the Export Inspection Council. See the [shrimp guide](/guide/how-to-export-shrimp-from-india).
Joining a general body when your product has a specific council or board.
Letting the RCMC lapse just before applying for Advance Authorisation or booking a council fair.
Exporting spices or APEDA products on the strength of an IEC alone.
Name, address or exporter type on the RCMC that differs from the IEC.
paras: Product-wise steps are in the guides for [leather footwear](/guide/how-to-export-leather-footwear-from-india), [garments](/guide/how-to-export-garments-from-india) and [brass and handicrafts](/guide/how-to-export-brass-and-handicrafts-from-india). Check what else you need with the [export readiness check](/tools/export-readiness).
Exportwalla's desk can do this paperwork with you, shipment by shipment, and you review and sign every filing; see [pricing](/pricing) or [talk to us](/contact).

faqs: Is RCMC compulsory for every exporter?

Not for every product. You can export most goods with only an IEC. But you need an RCMC to claim most Foreign Trade Policy benefits, and registration with APEDA, the Spices Board or MPEDA is compulsory before exporting their products.
How long is an RCMC valid?
Normally five years, counted from 1 April of the year it was issued to 31 March five years later, unless the council says otherwise. Renew it online on the DGFT e-RCMC service before it expires.
Which council should a Moradabad brass exporter join?

Brass artware, decorative metal items and other handicrafts come under the Export Promotion Council for Handicrafts (EPCH). Industrial brass parts and fittings are engineering goods and come under EEPC India.
What does an RCMC cost?

Each council sets its own registration fee and some add an annual subscription. APEDA, for example, charges ₹5,000 plus 18% GST for an RCMC valid five years. Check the fee on your council's page in the DGFT e-RCMC service before paying.
Can I hold RCMCs from two councils?
Yes. If you export products from different families, for example garments and home textiles, you can register with each council. Use the RCMC that matches the product for which you claim a benefit.
sources: DGFT: Handbook of Procedures, chapter 2 (paras 2.77–2.82, RCMC)
PIB: Export Promotion Mission and Market Access Support (Feb 2026)

hs-code-for-export.title: HS code for export: 6-digit HS, 8-digit ITC-HS, how to classify
hs-code-for-export.description: How the HS code, India's 8-digit ITC-HS and the buyer's tariff line fit together, how to classify a product, and why the code sets your duty.
hs-code-for-export.h1: HS code for export: find the right code before you quote
hs-code-for-export.answer: The HS code is the 6-digit product code every customs office in the world uses. India adds two digits (8-digit ITC-HS) on the shipping bill, and the buyer's country adds its own (UK and US use 10). Classify by reading the heading text and chapter notes under the General Rules of Interpretation. The code decides import duty, FTA eligibility and India's export incentive rates.

sections.h2: Three layers of the same code

head: Level
Digits
Who sets it
What it decides
rows: World Customs Organization; used by more than 200 countries
The common base. FTA rules of origin are written on it.
Shipping bill line, export policy (free or restricted), drawback and RoDTEP rates
Import duty, quotas, licences and product rules. UK and US use 10 digits, EU uses 8 (CN) and 10 (TARIC).

paras: The first six digits should be the same on your invoice, your shipping bill and the buyer's import entry. The digits after six are national and will differ. If the first six differ, one side has classified wrongly, and that is when customs asks questions.

sections.h2: How to classify, in plain words
paras: Classification follows six General Rules of Interpretation (GRIs) that every country applies the same way. In practice:
steps: Describe the product precisely: what it is made of, how it is made, what it does and how it is sold (single item, set, part).
Find the likely chapter, then read the four-digit heading text and the section and chapter notes. These are the law; chapter titles are only a guide (GRI 1).
An unfinished or unassembled article that already has the character of the finished one goes where the finished one goes (GRI 2).

If two headings fit, the more specific description wins. For mixtures and sets, the material or part that gives the essential character decides. If still tied, take the heading that comes last in number order (GRI 3).
If nothing fits, use the heading for the most similar goods (GRI 4). Normal packing and cases go with the goods (GRI 5).
Apply the same logic inside the heading to reach six digits, then pick India's eight-digit line (GRI 6).
Cross-check with India's tariff, the buyer's tariff and published rulings abroad.

bullets: **Moradabad brass statue for the home:** a decorative ornament of base metal goes to heading 8306 (statuettes and other ornaments), not to chapter 74 for copper and brass articles. The section notes keep chapter 83 articles out of chapter 74, so reading the notes settles it. (An original sculpture made by an artist is different: chapter 97.)
**Kanpur leather handbag with cotton lining:** heading 4202, and the subheading follows the outer surface material, here leather. The lining does not change it.
paras: Try your own product in the [HS code finder](/tools/hs-code-finder), or upload an invoice to the [free workspace](/app) and it suggests the code with duty and markets.

sections.h2: Why the code matters so much
bullets: **Duty abroad:** the buyer's duty is set per tariff line. See it with the [import duty tool](/tools/import-duty).

**FTA benefit:** a trade deal cuts duty only for lines in its schedule, and each line has its own rule of origin. See [trade agreements](/fta) and the [certificate of origin guide](/guide/certificate-of-origin).
**Indian export policy:** DGFT's ITC(HS) shows whether an item is free, restricted or prohibited for export.
**Incentives:** RoDTEP and drawback rates are listed per tariff line; see [RoDTEP and drawback](/guide/rodtep-and-duty-drawback).
**GST:** the GST rate on your inputs and supplies is also linked to the code.

sections.h2: Binding rulings: lock the code before a big order
paras: If the duty difference between two codes is large, get a binding ruling instead of arguing after the goods land.

**UK (ATaR):** an Advance Tariff Ruling from HMRC is legally binding on the commodity code and is generally valid for three years. The applicant needs a GB EORI number, so in practice your UK importer applies. HMRC replies in 30 to 120 days.

**EU (BTI):** a Binding Tariff Information decision is binding in every EU country for three years. The EU importer applies through the EU Customs Trader Portal with an EORI number; there is no fee for the decision itself.

**India:** the Customs Authority for Advance Rulings (benches in Delhi and Mumbai) can rule on the classification of goods before they are imported or exported. It is worth it when a restriction or a large incentive depends on the line.

bullets: Putting the buyer's 10-digit code on the Indian shipping bill instead of the Indian 8-digit line.
Copying a competitor's or supplier's code without reading the heading notes.
Choosing a line because its RoDTEP or drawback rate is higher. Misclassification leads to recovery with interest and penalties.
Vague invoice descriptions like 'handicraft items' or 'garments'. Write material, construction and use.
One code for a mixed set when the parts are sold separately.

faqs: Is the HS code the same in every country?

Only the first six digits. Every country that uses the Harmonized System shares the 6-digit code, then adds its own digits. India uses 8 digits, the UK and US use 10, and the EU uses 8 for its Combined Nomenclature and 10 for TARIC.
Which code goes on the Indian shipping bill?

The 8-digit Indian tariff item (ITC-HS). The buyer's 10-digit code belongs on their import declaration, though you can also show it on the invoice to help them. The first six digits of both should match.
Who decides the correct code?

The customs authority of each country, using the General Rules of Interpretation. Your declaration is your responsibility in India; the importer is responsible abroad. A binding ruling removes the doubt.
Can my buyer get a binding ruling in the UK or EU?

Yes. A UK importer with a GB EORI applies to HMRC for an Advance Tariff Ruling, generally valid three years. An EU importer applies for Binding Tariff Information, valid three years across the EU. Send them full product details and photos.
What happens if I use the wrong code?

Customs can reassess duty, recover incentives such as RoDTEP or drawback with interest, and levy penalties. Abroad, the buyer may lose the FTA rate and pay the full duty, which usually lands back on you as a claim.

certificate-of-origin.title: Certificate of origin in India: preferential vs non-preferential
certificate-of-origin.description: Preferential and non-preferential certificates of origin, applying on DGFT Trade Connect eCoO, self-declared origin under India–UK CETA, rules of origin.
certificate-of-origin.h1: Certificate of origin: which one you need and how to get it
certificate-of-origin.answer: A certificate of origin proves where goods were made. A preferential certificate lets your buyer pay the lower FTA duty; apply for it on DGFT's Trade Connect eCoO platform (trade.gov.in), issued by EIC, MPEDA, the Textiles Committee or another listed agency. A non-preferential certificate from a chamber or council only proves Indian origin. Some deals, such as India–UK CETA, also accept the exporter's own origin declaration.

What it does
Who issues it

paras: A non-preferential certificate never gets the buyer a lower duty. If the buyer wants the FTA rate, they need the preferential proof named in that agreement. Check your deal on the [trade agreements](/fta) page.

sections.h2: Rules of origin in plain words
paras: A preferential certificate is only valid if the product meets that agreement's rule of origin for its HS line. There are three common tests:
bullets: **Wholly obtained:** grown, mined, fished, or born and raised in India. Indian rice, cumin from Unjha and shrimp farmed in Andhra pass easily.

**Change of tariff classification:** imported materials must change heading (CTH, 4 digits), subheading (CTSH, 6 digits) or chapter. Imported finished leather (chapter 41) made into shoes (chapter 64) changes chapter.
**Value content:** a minimum share of the product's value must come from the partner countries. The percentage and the method are set line by line in each agreement.
**Never enough on their own:** simple operations such as packing, labelling, sorting or mixing.

**Tolerance:** a small share of non-originating material can be ignored. Under India–UK CETA it is 12.5% of value for industrial goods (chapters 25 to 98), and 7.5% or 12.5% by value or weight for farm and food chapters.

steps: Log in to trade.gov.in with your IEC-linked DGFT account. Keep your DSC or Aadhaar e-sign active in the profile.
Open Certificate of Origin and choose preferential or non-preferential, then the agreement and destination country.
Select the issuing agency: EIC, MPEDA or the Textiles Committee for preferential; a chamber or council for non-preferential.
Enter invoice details, the HS code and the origin criterion (wholly obtained, change of heading or value content), and upload the invoice plus cost sheet or input invoices where a value test applies.
Pay the agency fee online and submit. The agency may ask questions or inspect the goods.
Download the digitally signed eCoO with its QR code and send it to the buyer with the invoice before the goods arrive.
paras: Non-preferential certificates must be filed electronically on trade.gov.in since 1 January 2025, and preferential certificates are issued on the same eCoO platform. DGFT lists ₹600 for issuing a preferential certificate and ₹200 for each non-preferential certificate.

sections.h2: Self-declaration where the deal allows it
paras: **India–UK CETA (in force from 15 July 2026):** a UK importer can claim the lower duty with an origin declaration by the exporter or producer, a certificate from an issuing authority, or the importer's own knowledge backed by documents. The declaration follows the agreement's template, is in English, travels with the invoice and is valid for 12 months. On Trade Connect you can generate a self-declared eCoO for the UK without a fee, using a DSC linked to your IEC, or choose an agency instead. The UK can also waive proof for consignments up to £1,000 customs value. See [India–UK CETA](/fta/india-uk-ceta) and [exporting to the UK](/export-to/united-kingdom).

**EU GSP:** India has lost GSP for many industrial product groups for 2026–2028, but it still applies to others. Where it applies, the proof is a statement on origin on the invoice by an exporter registered in the REX system; consignments of originating goods up to €6,000 can carry a statement from any exporter. The [India–EU FTA](/fta/india-eu-fta) is a separate deal.

Most of India's other agreements, such as [India–UAE CEPA](/fta/india-uae-cepa) and [India–Australia ECTA](/fta/india-australia-ecta), work with agency-issued certificates. Check the deal page before you ship.

The importing country can verify origin months after the goods are cleared. Keep the bill of materials, input invoices, cost sheet, production records and supplier declarations for every shipment where you claimed origin. India–UK CETA requires exporters to keep them for five years. If you cannot prove origin, the buyer pays full duty and penalties, and you usually lose the customer.

bullets: Sending a non-preferential certificate when the buyer needs the preferential one.
HS code or invoice number on the certificate that differs from the invoice and shipping bill.
Claiming 'change of heading' without checking the product-specific rule for that line.
A trader declaring origin without the manufacturer's cost data to back it.
Claiming a deal for a line that is not in its tariff schedule.
paras: Check your line and the rule first with the [HS code guide](/guide/hs-code-for-export) and the [import duty tool](/tools/import-duty).

faqs: What is the difference between preferential and non-preferential certificates?

A preferential certificate is issued under a trade agreement and lets the buyer pay the lower agreement duty, if the goods meet its rules of origin. A non-preferential certificate only proves the goods are Indian and gives no duty cut.
Where do I apply for a certificate of origin in India?

On DGFT's Trade Connect platform, trade.gov.in, using your IEC-linked login. You choose the agreement and the issuing agency, fill in invoice and origin details, pay the fee and download a digitally signed eCoO.
Can I self-certify origin for UK exports?

Yes. Under India–UK CETA, the UK accepts an origin declaration completed by the exporter or producer. You can generate a self-declared eCoO on Trade Connect without a fee, with a DSC linked to your IEC. Keep the proof of origin for five years.
How long is a certificate of origin valid?
It depends on the agreement. Under India–UK CETA, a certificate or origin declaration is valid for 12 months from issue or completion. Check the deal page for other agreements.
Which agency issues preferential certificates?

DGFT Appendix 2B lists agencies per agreement. The Export Inspection Council covers all goods, MPEDA covers marine products, and the Textiles Committee covers textiles and made-ups under most agreements.

gst-on-exports-lut-refund.title: GST on exports: LUT (RFD-11), IGST refund and ITC refund
gst-on-exports-lut-refund.description: Exports are zero-rated: file an LUT in GST RFD-11 or pay IGST and get it refunded through the shipping bill, plus why export refunds get stuck.
gst-on-exports-lut-refund.h1: GST on exports: LUT, IGST refund and ITC refund
gst-on-exports-lut-refund.answer: Exports are zero-rated under GST. Either file a Letter of Undertaking (form GST RFD-11) for the financial year and export without paying IGST, then claim refund of unused input tax credit in form RFD-01; or pay IGST on the export invoice and get it back automatically, because the shipping bill itself counts as the refund claim. Most stuck refunds come from invoice mismatches between the shipping bill and GSTR-1, or a missing EGM.
facts: GST RFD-11, once per financial year

sections.h2: Two ways to export under GST

head: Route 1: export under LUT
Route 2: pay IGST, claim refund
rows: No IGST on the invoice; it states supply under LUT without payment of IGST
Charge IGST on the export invoice and pay it in GSTR-3B (credit can be used)
No separate form: the shipping bill is the claim
Exporters with a large credit balance who want automatic refunds

paras: Pick one route per invoice and keep it consistent across the invoice, the shipping bill and GSTR-1. Mixing them is a common reason for blocked refunds.

steps: Log in to gst.gov.in and go to Services, User Services, Furnish Letter of Undertaking (LUT).
Select the financial year. The LUT covers that year and expires on 31 March, so file a new one each April before the first export.
Tick the declarations, give two witnesses' names and addresses, and sign with DSC or EVC.
Note the ARN. Quote the LUT reference on every export invoice under it.
paras: Any registered person can use an LUT, except one prosecuted for tax evasion above ₹250 lakh, who must give a bond with a bank guarantee instead. A 2017 CBIC circular treats the LUT as accepted if the officer does not act within three working days. Under the LUT, goods must leave India within three months of the invoice date. If they do not, you pay the IGST with interest within 15 days, and the LUT facility is withdrawn until you do.

sections.h2: IGST route: the shipping bill is your refund claim
paras: Under Rule 96 of the CGST Rules, the shipping bill is treated as the refund application once these conditions are met:
bullets: The shipping line or airline has filed the export manifest (EGM) covering your shipping bill.
You have filed a valid GSTR-3B for the month, paying at least the IGST shown on the exports.
GSTR-1 Table 6A lists each export invoice with the same number, date and value as on the shipping bill.
You have completed Aadhaar authentication on the GST portal.
Your bank account is registered with customs at the port, so the refund has somewhere to land.
steps: GSTN sends your Table 6A data to ICEGATE.
Customs matches it with the shipping bill and EGM.
If everything matches, a refund scroll is generated and the money goes to your registered bank account.
Check the status on ICEGATE; error codes tell you what failed.

sections.h2: LUT route: refund of unused credit in RFD-01
steps: On the GST portal, file RFD-01 for refund of accumulated input tax credit on exports without payment of tax. You can cover one or several tax periods.
Upload the statement of export invoices with shipping bill numbers, dates and EGM details.
Work out the eligible amount: zero-rated turnover × net input tax credit ÷ adjusted total turnover. Credit on capital goods is left out of net ITC.
File within two years of the relevant date. For goods sent by sea or air, that is the date the ship or aircraft leaves India.
The officer can sanction 90% as a provisional refund within seven days of acknowledgement for zero-rated supplies, with the final order due within 60 days of a complete application.

bullets: **Invoice mismatch (ICEGATE code SB005):** the invoice number in GSTR-1 differs from the one on the shipping bill. If GSTR-1 is wrong, amend it through Table 9A. If the shipping bill is wrong, take it up with customs at the port.
**EGM not filed or faulty (SB002; SB006 for ICD gateway EGM):** ask the shipping line or your forwarder to file or correct it.
**GSTR-3B short:** IGST claimed in Table 6A is more than the IGST paid in GSTR-3B for that month.
**Bank account not validated:** the account registered with customs fails validation, so the scroll cannot be paid.
**Wrong route:** IGST charged on the invoice but the shipping bill filed under LUT, or the other way round.
**Aadhaar authentication pending** on the GST portal.

sections.h2: Where e-BRC and FIRC come in
paras: When the buyer's payment arrives, your bank sends the remittance details to DGFT, and you self-certify and generate the e-BRC against that remittance on DGFT's e-BRC system (the bank may also give you a FIRA or FIRC). For goods, the refund itself rests on the shipping bill and EGM. But if payment is not received within the period RBI allows, the GST refund has to be paid back with interest. Service exporters need the bank realisation proof to claim at all. Reconcile e-BRCs with shipping bills every month.

Related: [payment terms](/guide/letter-of-credit-and-payment-terms), [customs clearance](/guide/export-shipping-and-customs-clearance) and [RoDTEP and drawback](/guide/rodtep-and-duty-drawback). To work out your export price, use the [export price calculator](/tools/export-price-calculator).

faqs: Is GST charged on exports from India?

Exports are zero-rated. You either export under an LUT without paying IGST and claim refund of unused input credit, or pay IGST and get it refunded. Either way the tax does not stay in the export price.
How often do I file the LUT?
Once per financial year, on the GST portal in form RFD-11. It expires on 31 March, so file a fresh LUT in April before your first export invoice of the new year.
Do I need to file RFD-01 for an IGST refund on goods?

No. For goods exported on payment of IGST, the shipping bill is treated as the refund application once the EGM and a valid GSTR-3B are filed. RFD-01 is for refund of unused credit under an LUT, among other cases.
My IGST refund shows SB005. What does it mean?

SB005 means the invoice number on the shipping bill does not match the one in GSTR-1 Table 6A. Correct GSTR-1 through Table 9A if the return is wrong; if the shipping bill is wrong, approach the customs officer at the port of export.
What is the time limit for an ITC refund claim on exports?
Two years from the relevant date. For goods exported by sea or air, that is the date the ship or aircraft carrying them leaves India.

rodtep-and-duty-drawback.answer: RoDTEP refunds taxes built into your export price that no other scheme refunds, such as VAT on fuel, mandi tax and electricity duty, as a transferable duty credit e-scrip. All Industry Rate drawback refunds customs duty on inputs, in cash. You claim both through the shipping bill on ICEGATE. Rates differ by tariff line in DGFT Appendix 4R/4RE and CBIC's drawback schedule. RoDTEP is currently notified up to 31 December 2026.

**Drawback:** CBIC notifies the All Industry Rate schedule and amends it from time to time. Use the schedule in force on your shipping bill date.
**Brand rate:** if no All Industry Rate exists for your product, or it is far below the duty you actually paid, you can apply to the jurisdictional Commissioner for a brand rate with your cost data.

paras: RoDTEP and drawback can be a few percent of FOB, which matters on thin margins. faqs: Can I claim RoDTEP and drawback on the same shipment?

Yes, as a rule. Drawback refunds customs duty on inputs, while RoDTEP refunds other embedded taxes that are not refunded under any other scheme. Both are claimed in the same shipping bill, subject to each scheme's conditions.
Is RoDTEP available in 2027?

As of November 2026, RoDTEP is notified only up to 31 December 2026 (DGFT Notification 41/2026-27). Whether it continues after that depends on a new notification. Check the RoDTEP page on dgft.gov.in before quoting for 2027 shipments.
Where do I find the RoDTEP rate for my product?

In DGFT's Appendix 4R for exports from the Domestic Tariff Area, or Appendix 4RE for Advance Authorisation, SEZ and EOU exports, on the RoDTEP page of dgft.gov.in. Look up your exact 8-digit tariff item and any per-unit cap.
How is drawback paid?

All Industry Rate drawback is paid in cash to the bank account you registered with customs at the port, after the let export order and the EGM. The shipping bill itself is the claim, so no separate application is needed.
What can I do with a RoDTEP e-scrip?
Use it to pay basic customs duty on your own imports, or transfer it on ICEGATE to another importer, usually at a small discount. A scrip transfers in full, and it lapses after its expiry date.

export-pricing-fob-cif.title: Export pricing: how to calculate FOB and CIF prices
export-pricing-fob-cif.description: Build an export price step by step: ex-works cost, margin, packing, haulage and port charges to FOB, then freight and insurance to CIF and landed cost.
export-pricing-fob-cif.h1: How to build an export price: ex-works to FOB, CIF and the buyer's landed cost
export-pricing-fob-cif.answer: Start with your ex-works price: cost, margin and export packing. Add inland haulage, CHA, port and terminal handling charges to reach FOB. Add ocean freight and marine insurance to reach CIF. The buyer then adds import duty, import VAT or GST and destination charges to get landed cost. Exports under an LUT carry no GST, and RoDTEP or drawback should be kept as margin, not given away as discount.
facts: Nil when you export under LUT
Usually US$, with an FX buffer

sections.h2: The price ladder: EXW, FOB, CIF, landed cost
paras: Every export price is a ladder. Each rung adds a cost and moves the delivery point closer to the buyer. You quote one rung, and the buyer adds the rest. The rung you quote is your Incoterm, so read [Incoterms for Indian exporters](/guide/incoterms-for-indian-exporters) alongside this guide.

**EXW** (ex-works) is the goods packed at your gate. **FOB** adds the cost of getting them onto the vessel at the Indian port. **CIF** adds sea freight and insurance to the buyer's port. **Landed cost** is what the buyer finally pays once duty, import tax and local charges are added. Buyers compare suppliers on landed cost, so you should know it too.

sections.h2: Step by step: build your FOB price
steps: **Factory cost per unit.** Raw material, labour, power, overheads and wastage. Use actual costs from your last three months, not a hopeful estimate.
**Add your margin.** Decide it before you talk to the buyer. First orders are small and fussy, so do not cut margin to zero to win them.
**Add export packing and labelling.** Export cartons, pallets, shrink wrap, fumigation for wooden pallets, buyer's labels and barcodes. These are often forgotten.
**Add inland haulage.** Truck or rail from your factory to the port or ICD, for example Moradabad to Mundra or Tiruppur to Tuticorin. Get a written quote from your forwarder.

**Add CHA, port and terminal charges.** Customs broker (CHA) fee, terminal handling charges (THC) at origin, documentation, seal and any examination charges. The total of steps 1 to 5 divided by quantity is your FOB price per unit.

sections.h2: From FOB to CIF and the buyer's landed cost
bullets: **Ocean freight:** ask two or three forwarders for a rate to the buyer's port. Rates change often, so give your CIF quote a short validity, such as 15 days.
**Marine insurance:** under CIF the seller must insure at least 110% of the contract price on Institute Cargo Clauses (C) terms. Your insurer or forwarder quotes the premium.
**Import duty:** set by the buyer's country and your HS code. Check it with the [import duty tool](/tools/import-duty) and see whether a trade deal cuts it on the [FTA pages](/fta).
**Import VAT or GST:** most countries charge it on the customs value plus duty. A VAT-registered buyer usually recovers it later, but it still blocks cash at the border.
**Destination charges:** unloading, destination terminal fees, customs broker and delivery to the warehouse. The buyer's broker can tell you a typical figure.

**Customs value differs by country.** The EU and UK value goods on a CIF basis. The United States values imports broadly on the transaction price without international freight. This changes how much duty your price attracts.

paras: One 20-foot container of finished goods. The duty rate, VAT rate, freight and insurance figures below are **illustrative only**, not real quotes for any product or country. Run your own numbers in the [export price calculator](/tools/export-price-calculator).

bullets: Quote in the buyer's usual currency, most often US$, or EUR and GBP for Europe and the UK. Your costs are in ₹, so you carry the exchange risk between quote and payment.
Convert your ₹ costs at a rate slightly worse than today's rate. That cushion is your **FX buffer**. If the rupee strengthens before you are paid, the buffer protects your margin.
For larger orders, ask your bank about a forward contract to lock the rate for the expected payment date.
Add bank charges for the payment method. LCs and collections cost more than a plain advance transfer. See [letters of credit and payment terms](/guide/letter-of-credit-and-payment-terms).

sections.h2: GST, LUT and incentives: what goes in and what stays out
bullets: **No GST in the export price.** Exports are zero-rated. If you file a Letter of Undertaking (LUT), you export without paying IGST and claim back input tax. See [GST on exports, LUT and refund](/guide/gst-on-exports-lut-refund).

**RoDTEP and duty drawback are your margin, not the buyer's discount.** They arrive months later, can change, and can be recovered if payment is not realised. Price as if they were zero, then treat them as a bonus. See [RoDTEP and duty drawback](/guide/rodtep-and-duty-drawback).
**Common mistakes:** forgetting packing and fumigation, using last year's freight rate, quoting CIF without an insurance quote, and giving a long validity in a volatile freight market.
Exportwalla's desk can build the full quote with you, per shipment, while you stay exporter of record.

faqs: What is the difference between FOB and CIF price?

FOB covers your costs until the goods are loaded on the vessel at the Indian port. CIF adds ocean freight and marine insurance to the buyer's named port. Under both terms, risk passes to the buyer once the goods are on board in India. Only the cost split differs.
Should GST be added to my export price?

No. Exports are zero-rated. If you export under a Letter of Undertaking, you pay no IGST on the shipment and can claim a refund of input tax credit. Adding GST to a quote for a foreign buyer only makes your price look higher for no reason.
Should I pass RoDTEP to the buyer as a discount?

It is safer not to. RoDTEP and drawback reach you only after the shipment, rates can be revised, and the benefit can be recovered if export proceeds are not realised in time. Price as if they were zero and treat them as extra margin.
How much FX buffer should I keep?

There is no fixed rule. It depends on how long you wait for payment and how volatile the currency has been. Many small exporters convert their rupee costs at a rate a little below today's rate. For large orders, a bank forward contract is the cleaner option.
Why does the buyer care about landed cost?

Because that is what the goods actually cost them in their warehouse. A lower FOB price can still lose if your product attracts higher duty or freight than a competitor's. Knowing the landed cost also shows you when an FTA duty cut helps your offer.

faqs: FOB aur CIF price mein kya farak hai?

FOB mein aapka kharcha Indian port par jahaz par load hone tak hai. CIF mein buyer ke port tak ocean freight aur insurance bhi aap dete hain. Dono mein risk India mein jahaz par load hote hi buyer ka ho jaata hai.
Kya export price mein GST jodna chahiye?
Nahi. Export zero-rated hai. LUT par aap bina IGST export karte hain aur input tax credit ka refund le sakte hain. GST jodne se aapka price bina wajah mehnga dikhega.
Kya RoDTEP buyer ko discount mein de dein?
Behtar hai na dein. RoDTEP aur drawback shipment ke baad milte hain, rate badal sakte hain, aur samay par payment na aane par wapas liye ja sakte hain. Inhe zero maan kar price banayein.
FX buffer kitna rakhein?

incoterms-for-indian-exporters.description: Incoterms 2020 for small Indian exporters: EXW, FCA, FOB, CFR, CIF, DAP and DDP, where risk and cost pass, and which term to pick for a first order.
incoterms-for-indian-exporters.h1: Incoterms 2020 for Indian exporters: which term to quote and why
incoterms-for-indian-exporters.answer: Incoterms 2020 are ICC rules that fix who pays which costs and where risk passes from seller to buyer. Most small Indian exporters quote FOB or CIF for sea cargo, though ICC recommends FCA when goods are handed over in containers before loading. Under CIF you must insure at least 110% of the price on Institute Cargo Clauses (C). Avoid DDP on a first order: you would pay the buyer's import duty and tax.

sections.h2: What an Incoterm does, and what it does not
paras: An Incoterm is a three-letter code written after your price, such as **FOB Nhava Sheva** or **CIF Felixstowe**. It answers three questions: where you deliver, who pays which transport and clearance costs, and at what point the risk of loss or damage passes to the buyer.

It does **not** decide when you get paid, when ownership passes, or which law applies. Those belong in your sales contract and payment terms. Always name the exact place or port and write the version, for example FOB Mundra Incoterms 2020.

sections.h2: Risk and cost pass at different points under C terms
paras: This is the most misunderstood part. Under **CFR and CIF**, you pay freight all the way to the buyer's port, but the risk passes to the buyer when the goods are loaded on board in India. If the ship is delayed or cargo is damaged at sea, it is the buyer's loss, and the buyer claims on the insurance you bought.

Under **CIF**, the default insurance is the minimum Institute Cargo Clauses (C), for at least 110% of the contract price, in the contract currency. ICC (C) covers major events such as fire, sinking and stranding, but not most handling damage or theft. If your goods are fragile, such as glassware or brassware, agree ICC (A) with the buyer and price it in.

sections.h2: FOB or FCA for container shipments?
paras: Most Indian exporters write FOB even for full containers. ICC's own guidance is that FOB is not ideal when goods are in containers, because you hand the box to the carrier at the terminal or ICD, often days before it is loaded. Under FOB you still carry the risk until it is on board, though it is out of your control.

**FCA** fixes this. Risk passes when you hand the goods to the buyer's carrier at the named place, such as your factory, a CFS or the ICD. Incoterms 2020 also lets the parties agree that the buyer's carrier will issue an on-board bill of lading to the seller, which helps when your letter of credit asks for one.

sections.h2: How to choose: a simple rule for a first order
steps: **Default to FOB or FCA** if the buyer has a forwarder in India. You deliver locally and your risk ends early.
**Offer CIF or CFR** if the buyer wants a delivered-to-port price or you can get a good freight rate. Get a written freight and insurance quote before quoting.
**Avoid EXW**: as the Indian exporter you will still need to file the shipping bill to claim GST refund and incentives, so FCA at your factory is cleaner.

**Avoid DDP** until you know the market. You would pay import duty and VAT, may need a tax registration in the buyer's country, and carry customs delays that you cannot control. A wrong HS code or valuation becomes your cost.
**Match your documents.** The Incoterm on the invoice, contract, LC and insurance certificate must be identical. Mismatches are a common LC discrepancy.

paras: Each term needs a different price. FOB includes haulage and port costs, CIF adds freight and insurance, and DDP adds duty and tax. Use the [export pricing guide](/guide/export-pricing-fob-cif) and the [export price calculator](/tools/export-price-calculator) so the number matches the term. Exportwalla's desk can check your term and quote per shipment while you stay exporter of record.

faqs: Which Incoterm is best for a new Indian exporter?

FOB or FCA for most first orders, because your responsibility ends in India. CIF is fine for sea cargo if you have a firm freight and insurance quote. Avoid DDP until you know the buyer's market, since you would pay their import duty and tax.
Does CIF mean I am responsible until the goods reach the buyer?

No. Under CIF you pay freight and insurance to the destination port, but the risk passes to the buyer once the goods are loaded on board at the Indian port. If anything happens at sea, the buyer claims on the insurance policy you arranged.
What insurance must I buy under CIF?

Incoterms 2020 requires at least Institute Cargo Clauses (C) cover, for at least 110% of the contract price, in the contract currency. The buyer can ask for wider cover, such as ICC (A), at their cost or in the agreed price.
Why does ICC prefer FCA over FOB for containers?

Because with containers you hand the goods to the carrier at a terminal or ICD, before loading. Under FOB, the risk stays with you until the goods are on board, even though you no longer control them. FCA passes the risk at the handover point.
Do Incoterms decide when I get paid?

No. Incoterms deal with delivery, costs and risk. Payment, ownership and governing law must be written in your sales contract. Choose your payment method separately, such as advance, LC or collection.

**EXW se bachein**: GST refund aur incentives ke liye shipping bill aapko hi file karna hoga, isliye factory par FCA behtar hai.
**DDP se bachein**: buyer ke desh ki duty aur VAT aap par aayegi, wahan tax registration bhi lag sakta hai.
Invoice, contract, LC aur insurance par same Incoterm likhein. Price ke liye [export pricing guide](/hi/guide/export-pricing-fob-cif) dekhein.

faqs: Naye exporter ke liye kaunsa Incoterm sabse achha hai?

Kya CIF mein maal pahunchne tak risk mera hai?
Nahi. CIF mein freight aur insurance aap dete hain, par risk Indian port par jahaz par load hote hi buyer ka ho jaata hai. Raste mein nuksaan par buyer insurance claim karta hai.
CIF mein kaunsa insurance lena hai?
Incoterms 2020 ke hisaab se kam se kam Institute Cargo Clauses (C), contract price ke 110% par, contract ki currency mein. Buyer chahe to ICC (A) jaisa wider cover maang sakta hai.
Kya Incoterm se payment ka samay tay hota hai?

Nahi. Incoterm sirf delivery, kharcha aur risk batata hai. Payment ka samay, ownership aur kanoon sales contract mein likhne hote hain. Payment method, jaise advance, LC ya collection, alag se chunein.

letter-of-credit-and-payment-terms.answer: With a new buyer, ask for advance payment or a confirmed letter of credit. Documentary collection (D/P) is riskier, D/A riskier still, and open account is the riskiest, so never ship on open credit to an unknown buyer. LCs follow ICC's UCP 600 and pay only for documents that match exactly. Under RBI's 2026 export regulations, export proceeds must normally be realised within nine months of shipment.

sections.h2: Letters of credit: the basics of UCP 600
bullets: An LC is a bank's promise to pay you if you present documents that comply with its terms. Most LCs are issued subject to ICC's **UCP 600**, in force since 2007.
Banks check documents, not goods. Each bank has up to **five banking days** after presentation to decide whether documents comply.
Unless the LC says otherwise, documents must be presented within **21 calendar days** after shipment, and before the LC expires.
**Sight LC** pays when compliant documents are presented. **Usance LC** pays after a set period, such as 60 or 90 days, which you can often discount with your bank.
**Confirmed LC**: a second bank, usually in India, adds its own promise. This protects you if the buyer's bank or country cannot pay. It costs a confirmation fee.
Ask your bank to check the draft LC before the buyer issues it. Refuse terms you cannot meet, such as a shipment date too close or a certificate you cannot get.

sections.h2: Common LC discrepancies, and how to avoid them
bullets: Late shipment, or documents presented after 21 days or after expiry.
Goods description on the invoice not matching the LC wording.
Bill of lading without an on-board notation, or marked with damage (not clean).

Invoice amount or quantity above the LC limit. If the LC says "about" or "approximately", 10% either way is allowed. Otherwise a 5% quantity tolerance applies only when the LC does not count the goods in packages or pieces, and the invoice total still cannot exceed the LC amount.
Names, addresses, ports or the Incoterm differing between documents.
Insurance dated after shipment, or for less than the required value.
A missing document, signature or number of originals.
Fix: prepare a checklist from the LC on day one, and have your bank or CHA check the set before presenting. A discrepant LC loses its bank guarantee and the buyer can refuse.

paras: Under **D/P** and **D/A**, your bank sends the documents to the buyer's bank under ICC's collection rules (URC 522). Banks do not guarantee payment. Under D/P, an unpaid buyer cannot take the goods, but you may face port charges, demurrage and a forced resale. Under D/A, the buyer gets the goods first and you rely on their promise.

**Open account** means you trust the buyer fully. It is common with large retailers, but a first-time exporter should not ship on open credit to a new buyer. If you must offer credit, cover it with [ECGC export credit insurance](/guide/ecgc-export-credit-insurance) and a credit limit on that buyer.

sections.h2: FEMA rules: getting the money home on time
steps: **Route payment through your bank (AD bank).** The shipping bill and export declaration feed into RBI's EDPMS, and your bank closes each entry when money arrives.

**Realise within the time limit.** The Foreign Exchange Management (Export and Import of Goods and Services) Regulations, 2026, in force from 1 October 2026, set nine months from the date of shipment for goods, or twelve months if invoiced or settled in rupees. Your bank can extend this on a reasoned request. For shipments made before 1 October 2026, ask your AD bank which period applies.

**Unrealised bills have consequences.** If payment stays outstanding more than one year past the due date (or any extension your bank allowed), you can export further only against full advance or an irrevocable LC. Drawback and RoDTEP can be recovered and IGST refunds paid back.
**Generate e-BRC.** Banks send inward remittance data to DGFT, and you generate the e-BRC on the DGFT portal against it. It is your proof of realisation for incentives and audits.

sections.h2: A practical plan for your first orders
bullets: First order: 30 to 50% advance with the balance against documents, or a confirmed sight LC.
After two or three clean orders: unconfirmed LC or D/P.
Only with ECGC cover and history: D/A or open account.
Exportwalla's desk can check an LC draft and document set with you per shipment while you stay exporter of record.

faqs: What is the safest payment term for a new export buyer?

Full or part advance is safest. A confirmed letter of credit at sight is next, because a bank in India also promises to pay against compliant documents. Avoid D/A and open account with buyers you have not traded with before.
What is the difference between sight and usance LC?

A sight LC pays as soon as compliant documents are presented and checked. A usance LC pays after an agreed period, such as 90 days from the bill of lading date. You can often get the usance amount early by discounting it with your bank, at a cost.
Why do banks refuse LC documents?

Because of discrepancies: late shipment or presentation, invoice wording differing from the LC, a bill of lading without an on-board notation, amounts above the limit, or inconsistent names and ports. Under UCP 600 banks look only at documents, so small mismatches matter.
How long do I have to bring export money into India?

Under RBI's 2026 export regulations, nine months from the date of shipment for goods, or twelve months if the export is invoiced or settled in rupees. Your bank can extend the period on request. Check with your AD bank, as RBI amended these limits during 2025 and 2026.
What is an e-BRC and why does it matter?

An electronic Bank Realisation Certificate, generated on the DGFT portal against remittance data sent by your bank. It proves you were paid for the export. It is used to support incentive claims and refunds and to show FEMA compliance.
sources: ICC Academy: avoiding common LC discrepancies
RBI: Export and Import of Goods and Services Regulations, 2026 (as amended)

ecgc-export-credit-insurance.title: ECGC export credit insurance for small exporters
ecgc-export-credit-insurance.description: How ECGC protects Indian exporters from buyer default and country risk: Small Exporters Policy, SCR, buyer credit limits, premium, claims, bank cover.
ecgc-export-credit-insurance.h1: ECGC export credit insurance: cover against buyer default and country risk
ecgc-export-credit-insurance.answer: ECGC, the Government of India's export credit insurer, pays you most of your loss if a foreign buyer goes insolvent, does not pay, or if war or transfer restrictions block payment. Exporters with turnover up to ₹5 crore can take the Small Exporters Policy, covering 95% of commercial and 100% of political losses. You need an ECGC credit limit on each buyer. Premium depends on payment terms and the buyer's country.

paras: ECGC Ltd is a Government of India enterprise that insures exporters against non-payment. Cover starts from the date of shipment. If the buyer withholds payment over a quality, quantity or delivery dispute, ECGC does not pay unless you first get a final court judgment against the buyer in the buyer's country. Exchange-rate losses, and losses a normal marine cargo policy would cover, are also outside it.
bullets: **Commercial (buyer) risk:** buyer insolvency, buyer not paying for an extended period after the due date, and buyer refusing to take the goods, subject to conditions.
**LC bank risk:** the bank that opened the letter of credit failing or not paying.

**Political (country) risk:** the buyer's government blocking or delaying transfer of money, war or civil disturbance, new import bans or cancelled import licences, and extra freight from a diverted voyage.

sections.h2: Which policy suits a small exporter

head: Feature
Small Exporters Policy (SEP)
Shipments Comprehensive Risks (SCR)
rows: Expected export turnover up to ₹5 crore a year
Linked to a roughly four-month default period

paras: Both policies run for 12 months, offer a 5% no-claim bonus each claim-free year up to 50%, and require monthly declarations by the 15th of the next month. ECGC also offers buyer-wise and other specialised policies; ask a branch which fits your trade.

sections.h2: Buyer credit limits: the step people skip
paras: A policy alone does not cover a buyer. You must obtain a **credit limit** from ECGC on each buyer (and on LC-opening banks). ECGC assesses the buyer and approves the maximum it will cover. Ship above the limit and the excess is uninsured.

Apply before the first shipment, using ECGC's credit limit application form, with the buyer's full legal name, address, bank and expected order value. The Small Exporters Policy also allows discretionary limits on some buyers, subject to policy conditions. A refused or reduced limit is a useful warning about the buyer.

ECGC does not publish one flat rate. The premium rate depends on your **payment terms** (an LC costs less to cover than D/A or open account), the **credit period**, and the **country classification** of the buyer's market. You pay premium in advance and keep a premium deposit based on projected turnover, subject to the minimum premium above. Ask the nearest ECGC branch for a quote on your actual buyers and terms, and add the cost to your [export price](/guide/export-pricing-fob-cif).

steps: **Declare every shipment** monthly, by the 15th of the following month, and pay premium on time. Undeclared shipments are not covered.
**Report overdue bills** by the 15th of the next month once they cross the reporting limit (60 days past due under SEP, 30 days under SCR).
**Act to reduce the loss.** Follow up with the buyer, hold goods if possible, and take recovery steps, including legal action where advised.
**File the claim** within 360 days of the bill's due date or 540 days from policy expiry, whichever is earlier, with shipping documents, correspondence and proof of default.
**Share recoveries.** Money recovered from the buyer later is shared with ECGC in proportion to the loss each bore.

sections.h2: Cover for your bank's packing credit
paras: Separately, ECGC insures **banks** that lend to exporters under its Export Credit Insurance for Banks (ECIB) covers, for packing credit and post-shipment credit. The bank takes this cover, not you, and it protects the bank if you default. It makes banks more willing to lend to small exporters. ECGC's published literature lists normal cover of two-thirds of the loss for individual packing credit. Ask your bank whether your account is covered and whether the premium is passed on.

ECGC cover works best alongside sensible [payment terms](/guide/letter-of-credit-and-payment-terms) and a [checked buyer](/guide/how-to-find-export-buyers). Exportwalla's desk can help you prepare the credit limit application per shipment while you stay exporter of record.

faqs: Who is eligible for the ECGC Small Exporters Policy?

An exporter whose expected export turnover for the next year does not exceed ₹5 crore. ECGC describes it as suited to exporters with exposure of up to about ₹50 lakh on a single buyer. Exporters above ₹5 crore turnover use the Shipments Comprehensive Risks policy.
How much of my loss will ECGC pay?

Under the Small Exporters Policy, 95% of losses from commercial risks and 100% from political risks. Under the Shipments Comprehensive Risks policy, 90%. You must have declared the shipment, paid premium and held a valid credit limit on the buyer.
What does ECGC cover cost?

There is no single published rate. The premium depends on payment terms, credit period and the buyer's country classification. The Small Exporters Policy has a minimum premium of ₹5,000 for the policy period. Ask an ECGC branch for a quote on your buyers.
Do I need ECGC if I ship against a letter of credit?

Often not for that shipment, which is why LC-backed shipments can be excluded from the whole-turnover policies. ECGC can still cover the risk of the LC-opening bank failing to pay. It is most useful when you offer D/P, D/A or open account terms.
When must I file an ECGC claim?

Within 360 days of the due date of the export bill, or 540 days from the expiry of the policy cover, whichever is earlier. Before that you must have reported the overdue bill on time and taken steps to recover the money.
sources: ECGC: Export Credit Insurance for Banks

**LC bank risk:** LC kholne wala bank fail ho ya paisa na de.
**Country risk:** buyer ke desh mein paisa bhejne par rok, yudh, naya import ban ya licence cancel.

Buyer quality, quantity ya delivery par vivaad karke paisa roke, to ECGC tabhi deta hai jab aap buyer ke desh ki court se final judgment le aayein. Exchange rate ka nuksaan aur normal marine insurance wale nuksaan bhi cover nahi hote.

Sirf policy se buyer cover nahi hota. Har buyer par ECGC se **credit limit** leni hoti hai. Limit se zyaada maal bheja to woh hissa cover nahi hoga. Pehli shipment se pehle buyer ka poora naam, address, bank aur order value dekar apply karein. Limit kam ya mana ho to yeh buyer ke baare mein chetavani hai.

ECGC ek fixed rate publish nahi karta. Premium aapke **payment terms**, **credit period** aur buyer ke **desh ki category** par depend karta hai. Premium advance mein dena hota hai. Asli quote ke liye nazdeeki ECGC branch se poochhein aur yeh kharcha [export price](/hi/guide/export-pricing-fob-cif) mein jodein.

steps: Har shipment har mahine 15 tareekh tak declare karein aur premium samay par dein.
Overdue bill samay par report karein (SEP mein 60 din, SCR mein 30 din baad).
Nuksaan kam karne ke kadam uthaayein: buyer se follow-up, recovery, zaroorat ho to legal action.
Claim bill ki due date se 360 din, ya policy khatam hone se 540 din, jo pehle ho, ke andar file karein.
Baad mein recover hua paisa ECGC ke saath share karein.

sections.h2: Bank ke packing credit ka cover
paras: ECGC banks ko bhi ECIB cover deta hai, packing credit aur post-shipment loan par. Yeh bank leta hai aur aapke default par bank ko bachata hai. Apne bank se poochhein ki aapka account covered hai ya nahi. Sahi [payment terms](/hi/guide/letter-of-credit-and-payment-terms) ke saath ECGC sabse achha kaam karta hai. Exportwalla ka desk har shipment par credit limit application mein madad karta hai, exporter of record aap rehte hain.

faqs: ECGC Small Exporters Policy kaun le sakta hai?

Jiska agle saal ka expected export turnover ₹5 crore se zyaada nahi hai. ECGC ise ek buyer par lagbhag ₹50 lakh tak ke exposure wale exporter ke liye theek maanta hai. Isse bade exporter SCR policy lete hain.
ECGC nuksaan ka kitna hissa deta hai?
Small Exporters Policy mein commercial risk par 95% aur political risk par 100%. SCR policy mein 90%. Shart yeh hai ki shipment declare ki ho, premium diya ho aur buyer par valid credit limit ho.
ECGC cover ka kharcha kitna hai?
Ek fixed rate nahi hai. Premium payment terms, credit period aur buyer ke desh ki category par depend karta hai. SEP ka minimum premium ₹5,000 hai. Apne buyers ke liye ECGC branch se quote lein.
ECGC claim kab tak file karna hai?
Export bill ki due date se 360 din, ya policy cover khatam hone se 540 din, jo bhi pehle ho. Usse pehle overdue bill samay par report kiya ho aur recovery ke kadam uthaaye hon.

how-to-find-export-buyers.title: How to find export buyers for your product from India
how-to-find-export-buyers.description: Find real overseas buyers: importers of your HS code, Indian mission commerce wings, EPC buyer-seller meets, trade fairs, and how to verify a buyer.
how-to-find-export-buyers.h1: How to find export buyers: channels that work, and how to check a buyer
how-to-find-export-buyers.answer: Start with companies that already import your HS code: the UK's HMRC publishes importer names by commodity code, and shipment data covers other markets. Then use Indian missions' commerce wings, your export promotion council's buyer-seller meets and trade fairs, which the government's Market Access Support scheme helps fund. Treat B2B platforms with caution. Verify every buyer in its company registry, start with a small order, and take advance or LC payment.

sections.h2: Before you search: know your HS code and target market
paras: Buyers are found by product code, not by product name. Fix your HS code first with the [HS code finder](/tools/hs-code-finder) and the [HS code guide](/guide/hs-code-for-export). Then pick two or three markets where your code is imported in volume and duty is low; an FTA such as the [India–UK CETA](/fta/india-uk-ceta) can help. Check yourself with the [export readiness tool](/tools/export-readiness), and keep your [IEC](/guide/how-to-get-iec-code) and [RCMC](/guide/rcmc-export-promotion-council) ready, because serious buyers ask.

steps: **Importers who already buy your HS code.** They know the product, the duty and the paperwork. In the UK, HMRC's uktradeinfo service lets you search traders by commodity code and publishes importer names and addresses (not values). For other markets, customs shipment data is sold by private providers; use it to list importers, then check them yourself. See [exporting to the United Kingdom](/export-to/united-kingdom).

**Commerce wings of Indian missions.** Indian embassies and high commissions have commerce or trade sections that pass on trade enquiries, share importer lists and help at fairs. Write to the commercial officer with your product, HS code and capacity. Trade enquiries received by missions are also posted on the Indian Trade Portal.

**Your export promotion council.** EPCs run buyer-seller meets in India and abroad, reverse buyer-seller meets where buyers visit India, and India pavilions at trade fairs. These are mainly for member exporters with an RCMC.

**International trade fairs.** The best place to meet many buyers in a few days. The government's Export Promotion Mission now funds trade fairs, buyer-seller meets, reverse buyer-seller meets and trade delegations through its Market Access Support (MAS) intervention, which replaced the earlier Market Access Initiative (MAI) scheme, with airfare support for MSMEs at eligible events. Ask your EPC which events are supported this year.

**B2B platforms.** Useful for visibility, but full of price shoppers, fake buyers and scams. Never pay a fee to receive an order, and never ship on credit to a buyer who found you there. Treat a platform enquiry as a lead to verify, not as an order.

sections.h2: How to verify a buyer before you ship
bullets: **Company registry.** Check the legal name, number, address and status. In the UK, Companies House is free online; most countries have an equivalent. A buyer who is not registered, or whose name differs from the email, is a red flag.
**Do they import your product?** Look for them in importer data for your HS code.
**Website, address and phone.** Use maps and call the switchboard, not only the mobile number in the email.
**References.** Ask for a supplier or bank reference, and check with the Indian mission's commerce wing if unsure.
**ECGC credit limit.** If you will offer credit, an [ECGC](/guide/ecgc-export-credit-insurance) limit request also tests the buyer.
**Small first order on safe terms.** Advance or a confirmed LC. See [payment terms](/guide/letter-of-credit-and-payment-terms).
**Warning signs:** urgency, free email domains, requests to change bank details, sample fees paid to the buyer, or pressure to ship before payment.

sections.h2: A first email that gets replies
steps: **Subject line with product and HS code**, for example: Brass planters, HS 7419, manufacturer in Moradabad.
**Two lines on who you are**: manufacturer, years in business, capacity per month, certifications.
**Why them**: mention the product range they already import.
**One clear offer**: a price indication on FOB or CIF terms, minimum order, lead time and sample availability.
**Proof**: three photos or a short catalogue link, not a heavy attachment.

**One question to answer**, such as: Shall I send samples for your spring range? Then follow up once after a week. Do not send the same mass email to hundreds of addresses; ten researched emails beat a thousand generic ones.

sections.h2: Turn interest into a safe first order
paras: Agree the price on a named Incoterm, using the [export pricing guide](/guide/export-pricing-fob-cif). Send a proforma invoice, take advance or an LC, and keep the first order small. Exportwalla's free [workspace](/app) reads your invoice and suggests HS code, markets, duty, likely buyers, a quote and documents; its desk can run outreach with you per shipment while you stay exporter of record.

faqs: What is the most reliable way to find export buyers?

Target companies that already import your HS code into your chosen market. They understand the product and the import process. The UK publishes importer names by commodity code through HMRC; for other countries, shipment data from private providers can give a starting list that you then verify.
Can Indian embassies help me find buyers?

Yes. Indian missions abroad have commerce or trade sections that pass on trade enquiries, share importer contacts and support Indian participation in fairs. Write to the commercial officer with your product, HS code, capacity and certifications. Some enquiries are also posted on the Indian Trade Portal.
Is there government support for attending trade fairs?

Yes. Under the Export Promotion Mission, the Market Access Support intervention, which replaced the older Market Access Initiative scheme, funds trade fairs, buyer-seller meets and trade delegations, with airfare support for MSMEs at eligible events. Supported events change each year, so ask your EPC which ones are covered.
Are B2B platforms worth using?

They can bring enquiries, but quality is mixed and scams are common. Never pay a fee to receive an order, verify every buyer in its company registry, and ask for advance or LC payment on any order that comes through a platform.
How do I check that a foreign buyer is genuine?

Check the company registry, confirm they import your product, call their listed switchboard, ask for references, and keep the first order small with advance or a confirmed LC. Red flags include free email addresses, urgency and requests to change bank details.
sources: PIB: Export Promotion Mission, Market Access Support (Feb 2026)

hi.answer: Un companies se shuru karein jo pehle se aapka HS code import karti hain: UK mein HMRC commodity code ke hisaab se importer ke naam publish karta hai, baaki deshon ke liye shipment data hai. Phir Indian mission ke commerce wing, EPC ke buyer-seller meet aur trade fair, jinke liye sarkar ki Market Access Support scheme madad deti hai. B2B platform se saavdhaan rahein. Har buyer company registry mein check karein, chhota order lein aur advance ya LC lein.

sections.h2: Pehle HS code aur market tay karein
paras: Buyer product code se milte hain. [HS code finder](/tools/hs-code-finder) se code pakka karein aur do-teen market chunein jahan yeh code zyaada import hota hai aur duty kam hai, jaise [India–UK CETA](/fta/india-uk-ceta). [IEC](/hi/guide/how-to-get-iec-code) aur [RCMC](/hi/guide/rcmc-export-promotion-council) taiyaar rakhein.
