Dekhein [UK export page](/export-to/united-kingdom). Baaki deshon ke liye private shipment data se list banaayein aur khud check karein.
**Indian mission ke commerce wing.** Commercial officer ko product, HS code aur capacity likhkar bhejein. Missions ki trade enquiries Indian Trade Portal par bhi aati hain.
**Aapki export promotion council.** EPC buyer-seller meet, reverse buyer-seller meet aur trade fair mein India pavilion chalati hai, mukhya roop se RCMC wale member exporters ke liye.

**International trade fair.** Sarkar ke Export Promotion Mission ki Market Access Support (MAS) scheme, jo purani Market Access Initiative (MAI) ki jagah aayi hai, trade fair, buyer-seller meet aur trade delegation ke liye fund deti hai, aur MSMEs ko airfare support bhi. EPC se poochhein is saal kaunse event hain.
**B2B platform.** Visibility milti hai par fake buyer aur scam bhi bahut hain. Order ke liye kabhi fee na dein.

bullets: Company registry mein naam, number aur status dekhein. UK mein Companies House free hai.
Kya woh aapka product import karta hai? Importer data mein dhoondhein.
Website, address aur office ka phone number check karein.
Supplier ya bank reference maangein. Credit dena ho to [ECGC](/hi/guide/ecgc-export-credit-insurance) limit lein.
Pehla order chhota, advance ya confirmed LC par. Dekhein [payment terms](/hi/guide/letter-of-credit-and-payment-terms).
Khatre ke sanket: jaldbaazi, free email, bank details badalne ki request, payment se pehle shipment ka dabaav.

steps: Subject mein product aur HS code, jaise: Brass planters, HS 7419, Moradabad manufacturer.
Do line mein aap kaun hain: manufacturer, saal, monthly capacity, certificates.
Unhe kyon likh rahe hain: woh jo range import karte hain uska zikr.
Ek saaf offer: FOB ya CIF price, minimum order, lead time, sample.
Teen photo ya catalogue link, aur ek sawaal. Ek hafte baad ek follow-up.

sections.h2: Interest ko surakshit order mein badlein
paras: Price ek Incoterm par tay karein ([pricing guide](/hi/guide/export-pricing-fob-cif)), proforma invoice bhejein aur advance ya LC lein. Exportwalla ka free [workspace](/app) invoice padhkar HS code, market, duty, buyer, quote aur documents batata hai; desk har shipment par outreach mein saath deta hai, exporter of record aap rehte hain.

faqs: Export buyer dhoondhne ka sabse bharosemand tareeka kya hai?

Un companies ko target karein jo pehle se aapka HS code us market mein import karti hain. UK mein HMRC commodity code se importer ke naam publish karta hai. Doosre deshon mein private shipment data se list banaakar khud verify karein.
Kya Indian embassy buyer dhoondhne mein madad karti hai?

Haan. Videsh mein Indian missions ke commerce ya trade section trade enquiries aage bhejte hain, importer contacts dete hain aur fair mein madad karte hain. Commercial officer ko product, HS code aur capacity ke saath likhein.
Trade fair ke liye sarkari madad milti hai?

Haan. Export Promotion Mission ki Market Access Support scheme, jo purani MAI scheme ki jagah aayi hai, trade fair, buyer-seller meet aur trade delegation ke liye fund deti hai, aur MSMEs ko airfare support bhi. Har saal events badalte hain, EPC se poochhein.
Buyer asli hai, kaise pata karein?
Company registry check karein, dekhein ki woh aapka product import karta hai, office number par call karein, reference maangein, aur pehla order chhota rakhein advance ya confirmed LC ke saath.

export-shipping-and-customs-clearance.title: Export shipping and customs clearance in India, step by step
export-shipping-and-customs-clearance.description: How an export shipment leaves India: forwarder booking, FCL, LCL or air, stuffing, shipping bill on ICEGATE, AD code, examination, LEO, B/L and EGM.
export-shipping-and-customs-clearance.h1: Export shipping and customs clearance in India: from booking to bill of lading
export-shipping-and-customs-clearance.answer: Book space with a freight forwarder, choose FCL, LCL or air, and stuff the cargo at your factory or a CFS. Your CHA files the shipping bill on ICEGATE, after your AD code is registered at that port. Customs may examine the goods, then grants Let Export Order (LEO). The goods are loaded, the carrier issues the bill of lading, and the shipping line files the Export General Manifest (EGM).
facts: AD code registered at that port

sections.h2: Choose the mode: FCL, LCL or air

head: Mode
What it means
Best for
rows: You hire a whole container: 20-foot (about 33 cubic metres), 40-foot (about 67) or 40-foot high cube (about 76)
Large or heavy orders; lower cost per unit, less handling
Your cartons share a container with others, packed at a CFS
Small first orders; you pay by volume or weight but there is more handling and a few extra days
Shipped on an airline under an air waybill
Samples, urgent or high-value, light goods; costs several times sea freight

paras: Container capacities are approximate internal volumes; the cartons you can actually load usually fill less. Heavy goods such as rice or stone often hit the weight limit before the volume limit; ask your forwarder for the payload limit on your route.

sections.h2: Step by step: from booking to sailing
steps: **Book with a freight forwarder or shipping line.** Give cargo details, HS code, volume, weight, port and target vessel. You get a booking confirmation with vessel, cut-off times and the empty-container pick-up point. Under FOB or FCA the buyer's forwarder may book instead.

**Prepare documents.** Commercial invoice and packing list, matching the order and any LC. Add a [certificate of origin](/guide/certificate-of-origin) if the buyer wants FTA duty, and any inspection, phytosanitary or fumigation certificate your product needs.

**Register your AD code at the port.** Your bank's AD code and your bank account must be registered in the customs system at each port or ICD you export from. Without it, export proceeds and incentives cannot be linked to the shipping bill. You register it once per port on ICEGATE, with bank proof uploaded on e-SANCHIT, and customs at that port approves it; your CHA can help.

**Stuff the container.** **Factory stuffing**: the container comes to your premises, you load it, and it is sealed with an RFID e-seal under customs' self-sealing procedure. **CFS stuffing**: you truck cartons to a container freight station where they are packed, which is normal for LCL.

**CHA files the shipping bill on ICEGATE.** It carries your IEC, GSTIN, HS code, value, LUT or IGST details, drawback and RoDTEP claims, and the export declaration. Check the draft (checklist) carefully: errors here delay refunds and incentives.
**Customs assessment and examination.** The risk system decides whether goods are examined or cleared on documents. If selected, officers check the goods against the declaration.
**Let Export Order (LEO).** Once customs is satisfied it grants LEO. The goods can then be loaded. The LEO date is the date of export for most purposes.
**Loading and bill of lading.** After loading, the carrier issues the bill of lading (or air waybill). Check names, ports, description and the on-board date against your LC before accepting.
**EGM.** After sailing, the shipping line or agent files the Export General Manifest. Your shipping bill must match the EGM for IGST refunds and drawback to flow.

bullets: Commercial invoice and packing list.
Shipping bill (filed by your CHA on ICEGATE).
Bill of lading or air waybill.
Certificate of origin, if the buyer claims FTA duty or the market requires it.
Insurance certificate, if you sell CIF or CIP. See [Incoterms](/guide/incoterms-for-indian-exporters).
Product certificates as needed: inspection, phytosanitary, fumigation, health or quality.
LC documents, bill of exchange and bank forwarding letter where payment is by LC or collection.

paras: Plan backwards from the vessel cut-off. Book space well ahead, especially in peak season. Customs clearance usually takes a day or two when papers are right, longer if examination is ordered. Sea transit to Europe or the US takes weeks, so agree the shipment date with the buyer in the contract.
bullets: **Missed cut-off**: the container rolls to the next vessel, and an LC shipment date can be missed.
**Mismatch between invoice, packing list and shipping bill**: examination, delay, refund hold-ups.
**AD code not registered at that port**: export proceeds and incentives do not link.
**Wrong HS code**: wrong incentive rate, questions from customs, wrong duty for the buyer. Check it with the [HS code finder](/tools/hs-code-finder).
**No fumigation certificate for wooden packing**: the buyer's customs may hold the cargo.

sections.h2: At destination: the buyer's customs broker
paras: Under FOB, CIF or DAP, the buyer's customs broker clears the goods at destination, pays duty and import tax, and arranges delivery. Send scanned documents early and the originals (or a telex release or sea waybill) as agreed, so the cargo does not sit and attract demurrage. Under DDP this becomes your job, which is why first-time exporters avoid it.

Exportwalla's desk can coordinate the forwarder, CHA and documents with you per shipment, while you stay exporter of record. For the full picture, see [how to export from India](/guide/how-to-export-from-india).

faqs: Who files the shipping bill?

Usually your customs broker (CHA) files it electronically on ICEGATE using your IEC, GSTIN, invoice and packing list. You can file it yourself if registered, but most small exporters use a CHA. Check the draft checklist before filing, because errors delay refunds and incentives.
What is a Let Export Order?

LEO is customs' permission for the goods to be loaded for export. It is granted after the shipping bill is assessed and any examination is complete. The LEO date is generally treated as the date of export for incentives and other purposes.
Why do I need to register my AD code at the port?

Customs links each shipping bill to your bank through the AD code registered at that port. Without it, export proceeds cannot be tracked against the shipment and incentive or refund credits can get stuck. It is done once per port or ICD.
Should I choose FCL or LCL for my first order?

If your goods fill most of a 20-foot container, FCL is usually cheaper per unit and safer, with less handling. For a few pallets or cartons, LCL is more economical, but expect extra handling at the CFS and a few more days in transit.
What is the EGM and why does it matter?

The Export General Manifest is filed by the shipping line or airline after departure, listing the cargo carried. Customs matches your shipping bill against the EGM before IGST refunds and drawback are processed, so a mismatch holds your money.
sources: ICEGATE: AD code bank account registration advisory

hi.title: Export shipping aur customs clearance: step by step
hi.description: India se export shipment kaise nikalta hai: booking, FCL, LCL ya air, stuffing, ICEGATE par shipping bill, AD code, examination, LEO, B/L aur EGM.
hi.h1: Export shipping aur customs clearance: booking se bill of lading tak
hi.answer: Freight forwarder ke saath space book karein, FCL, LCL ya air chunein, aur maal factory ya CFS par container mein bharein. Port par AD code register hone ke baad CHA ICEGATE par shipping bill file karta hai. Customs maal check kar sakta hai, phir Let Export Order (LEO) deta hai. Maal jahaz par load hota hai, carrier bill of lading deta hai, aur shipping line Export General Manifest (EGM) file karti hai.

sections.h2: Mode chunein: FCL, LCL ya air

head: Mode
Matlab
Kab theek
rows: Poora container: 20-foot (lagbhag 33 cubic metre), 40-foot (lagbhag 67) ya 40-foot high cube (lagbhag 76)
Aapke cartons doosron ke saath CFS par container mein
Chhota pehla order, thode din zyaada
Sample, urgent ya mehnga halka maal

paras: Yeh andar ka lagbhag volume hai, asal mein cartons isse kam aate hain. Bhaari maal jaise chawal ya stone mein volume se pehle weight limit aa jaati hai, forwarder se payload limit poochhein.

sections.h2: Step by step: booking se sailing tak
steps: **Forwarder ya shipping line se booking.** HS code, volume, weight, port aur vessel batayein. Booking confirmation mein vessel, cut-off aur khaali container ki jagah milti hai. FOB ya FCA mein buyer ka forwarder bhi book kar sakta hai.
**Documents taiyaar karein.** Invoice aur packing list order aur LC se match karein. FTA duty ke liye [certificate of origin](/hi/guide/certificate-of-origin) aur zaroori certificates jodein.

**Port par AD code register karein.** Bank ka AD code aur account har port ya ICD par customs system mein register hona chahiye, warna payment aur incentive shipping bill se link nahi honge. Yeh ICEGATE par har port ke liye ek baar hota hai, bank proof e-SANCHIT par upload karke, aur us port ka customs approve karta hai. CHA madad kar sakta hai.

**Stuffing.** **Factory stuffing** mein container aapke yahan bharta hai aur self-sealing procedure mein RFID e-seal lagti hai. **CFS stuffing** mein cartons CFS par bharte hain, LCL mein yahi hota hai.
**CHA ICEGATE par shipping bill file karta hai** jismein IEC, GSTIN, HS code, value, LUT, drawback aur RoDTEP claim hote hain. Checklist dhyaan se check karein.
**Assessment aur examination.** Risk system tay karta hai ki maal khulega ya sirf documents par clear hoga.
**Let Export Order (LEO).** Customs santusht hone par LEO deta hai, phir loading hoti hai.
**Bill of lading.** Load hone ke baad carrier B/L deta hai. Naam, port, description aur on-board date LC se milaayein.
**EGM.** Jahaz nikalne ke baad shipping line EGM file karti hai. Shipping bill aur EGM match hone par hi IGST refund aur drawback aate hain.

bullets: Commercial invoice aur packing list.
Shipping bill (CHA ICEGATE par file karta hai).
Bill of lading ya air waybill.
Certificate of origin, jahan zaroori ho.
Insurance certificate, CIF ya CIP mein. Dekhein [Incoterms](/hi/guide/incoterms-for-indian-exporters).
Product certificates: inspection, phytosanitary, fumigation.
LC ya collection ke documents aur bill of exchange.

paras: Vessel cut-off se peechhe ki taraf plan karein. Sahi papers par customs clearance aam taur par ek-do din leti hai, examination ho to zyaada.
bullets: **Cut-off chhoota**: container agle jahaz par, LC ki shipment date chhoot sakti hai.
**Invoice, packing list aur shipping bill mein farak**: examination aur refund mein der.
**Galat HS code**: galat incentive rate aur buyer ki galat duty. [HS code finder](/tools/hs-code-finder) se check karein.
**Wooden packing ka fumigation certificate nahi**: buyer ke desh mein maal atak sakta hai.

paras: FOB, CIF ya DAP mein buyer ka customs broker wahan clearance karta hai aur duty deta hai. Documents jaldi bhejein taaki demurrage na lage. DDP mein yeh kaam aapka hota hai, isliye naye exporter ise avoid karte hain. Exportwalla ka desk har shipment par forwarder, CHA aur documents aapke saath sambhalta hai, exporter of record aap rehte hain.

faqs: Shipping bill kaun file karta hai?
Aam taur par aapka CHA ICEGATE par aapke IEC, GSTIN, invoice aur packing list se file karta hai. File karne se pehle checklist zaroor check karein, kyunki galti se refund aur incentive atakte hain.
Let Export Order kya hai?
LEO customs ki permission hai ki maal export ke liye load ho sakta hai. Yeh shipping bill assessment aur examination ke baad milta hai. LEO date ko aam taur par export ki date maana jaata hai.
Port par AD code register kyon karna hai?
Customs har shipping bill ko us port par registered AD code se aapke bank se jodta hai. Iske bina payment aur incentive link nahi hote. Yeh har port ya ICD par ek baar hota hai.
Pehle order ke liye FCL ya LCL?
Maal 20-foot container ka zyaadatar hissa bhar de to FCL per unit sasta aur surakshit hai. Kuchh cartons ya pallets ke liye LCL sasta hai, par CFS par handling aur kuchh din zyaada lagte hain.

how-to-export-leather-footwear-from-indi.title: How to export leather footwear from India: 2026 guide
how-to-export-leather-footwear-from-indi.description: Registrations, CLE membership, EU chromium VI and labelling rules, sampling, packing and payment terms for Indian leather shoe exporters.
how-to-export-leather-footwear-from-indi.h1: How to export leather footwear from India
how-to-export-leather-footwear-from-indi.answer: To export leather footwear from India you need an IEC, an RCMC from the Council for Leather Exports (CLE), the right HS code (heading 6403 for leather uppers, 6406 for uppers and parts) and shoes that pass the buyer's chemical tests, above all chromium VI in leather for the EU and UK. Most orders come from brands and importers who send a tech pack, approve samples and inspect before shipment.
facts: Chromium VI in leather touching skin: 3 mg/kg

sections.h2: What buyers abroad want and how they buy
paras: Most export orders come from brands, private-label importers and retail chains, not from walk-in wholesalers. They work in seasons (spring–summer and autumn–winter) and follow a fixed development path: tech pack, proto sample, fit and wear trials, salesman samples, then a bulk order with a minimum quantity per style and colour.

Each cluster has a reputation buyers already know. Agra is strong in men's formal shoes, moccasins and casuals; Ambur, Vaniyambadi and Chennai make finished shoes and uppers for European brands; Kanpur is known for heavy leather and safety footwear; Kolkata makes shoes and uppers. Lead with what your cluster does well.

Classification matters because the duty abroad depends on it. Leather-upper shoes fall under 6403, split by sole material and whether they cover the ankle, for example [640391](/hs-code/640391-leather-footwear-covering-the-ankle-outer-soles-of-rubber) and [640399](/hs-code/640399-leather-footwear-outer-soles-of-rubber-plastics-or). Uppers sold to other shoemakers go under [640610](/hs-code/640610-footwear-parts-uppers-and-thereof-other-than-stiffeners). The table below shows what each market charges.

bullets: **IEC** from DGFT: see [how to get an IEC](/guide/how-to-get-iec-code).
**RCMC from CLE**, which DGFT lists as the council for leather and leather products. You need it for export incentives and council support: see [RCMC](/guide/rcmc-export-promotion-council).
**GST LUT** so you can ship without paying IGST: see [GST on exports](/guide/gst-on-exports-lut-refund).
**AD code** registered with customs through your bank, plus an ICEGATE login for shipping bills.

sections.h2: Quality, testing and compliance by market
paras: **EU and UK:** REACH restricts chromium VI in leather articles that touch the skin to 3 mg/kg. That covers shoe uppers, linings and insocks, so test every leather lot, not just the first sample. REACH also bans certain azo dyes and dimethyl fumarate (DMF), the old anti-mould sachet chemical. Shoes sold to EU consumers must carry the labelling that Directive 94/11/EC requires: pictograms or words showing the material of the upper, the lining and sock, and the outer sole. The UK has its own footwear labelling rules on the same model.

**US:** each shoe must be permanently marked with the country of origin ("Made in India"), and buyers usually want the box marked too. US buyers test against their own restricted-substance lists, and many ask for California Proposition 65 compliance. The US tariff line depends on upper and sole material and construction, so agree the classification with the buyer's customs broker before costing. Since 24 July 2026 Indian footwear also pays an extra 10% US duty under Section 301, on top of the normal tariff.
**Gulf and other markets:** buyers usually set the standard themselves. Ask early whether the importer needs a conformity certificate for their market, and get it in the contract.

Many brands also want the tannery to hold a Leather Working Group (LWG) rating and the factory to pass a social audit. These are buyer requirements, not laws, but without them you will not get on many vendor lists.

bullets: Size label in the buyer's system (UK, EU or US). Size conversions are not interchangeable; use the buyer's grading chart.
Material label or pictograms for EU and UK orders; origin marking on shoe and box for the US.
Silica gel or other approved desiccant (never DMF), tissue and shoe trees as specified. Mould in monsoon shipments is a common claim.
Export cartons with the buyer's carton marks, pairs per carton, and gross and net weight. Keep a packing list per carton.

paras: Quote per pair, usually FOB Indian port or FCA factory, with leather, sole, components and labour costed separately so you can re-price when leather moves. Samples are normally charged, with the cost adjusted against the first order. New buyers commonly pay an advance with the balance against shipping documents or use a letter of credit; established retailers often ask for open-account terms, which is where [ECGC cover](/guide/ecgc-export-credit-insurance) helps. Use the [export price calculator](/tools/export-price-calculator) to build an FOB price.

bullets: Testing chromium VI only on the approved sample, then changing tannery for bulk.
Quoting before the HS code is agreed, so the buyer's landed cost is wrong.
Late delivery against the season. Brands often build penalties or cancellations for late shipment into the order.
Weak packing: crushed toes, mould and wrong carton marks cause claims even when the shoes are good.

steps: Get your IEC, GST LUT and CLE RCMC.
Confirm the HS code with the [HS code finder](/tools/hs-code-finder) and check duty in the table below or the [import duty tool](/tools/import-duty).
Get chromium VI and azo test reports from an accredited lab for your main leathers.
Find buyers through CLE fairs and buyer-seller meets: see [how to find export buyers](/guide/how-to-find-export-buyers).
Agree Incoterms and payment terms in writing: see [Incoterms](/guide/incoterms-for-indian-exporters) and [payment terms](/guide/letter-of-credit-and-payment-terms).

faqs: Which export council should a leather shoe maker join?

The Council for Leather Exports (CLE). DGFT's list of export promotion councils assigns leather and leather products, including footwear, to CLE. Its RCMC is what you show to claim export benefits and to take part in CLE trade fairs and buyer meets.
What is the chromium VI limit for leather shoes in Europe?

Under the EU REACH restriction, leather articles that come into contact with the skin may not contain chromium VI at 3 mg/kg or more. The UK applies the same limit. Test each leather lot at an accredited lab, because tanning and storage conditions change results.
Do I need to label materials on shoes sold in the EU?

Yes. Directive 94/11/EC requires footwear sold to consumers to show the material of the upper, the lining and sock, and the outer sole, using pictograms or written words. The importer or brand is responsible, but they will expect you to apply the labels at the factory.
Can I export shoe uppers instead of finished shoes?

Yes. Many Ambur, Vaniyambadi and Chennai units export uppers to shoemakers abroad. Uppers are classified under HS 640610, and the same chemical limits apply to the leather because it ends up in a finished shoe.
Is a social audit compulsory?

Not by law, but most brands will only place orders with factories that have passed a recognised social audit and, often, a tannery rating such as LWG. Ask the buyer which audit they accept before you pay for one.
sources: Federal Register: Section 301 forced-labour action and exemption annexes (28 Jul 2026)

how-to-export-leather-bags-from-india.title: How to export leather bags and goods from India
how-to-export-leather-bags-from-india.description: Handbags, wallets, travel goods and saddlery: CLE registration, HS codes, EU and US chemical and labelling rules, sampling and payment terms.
how-to-export-leather-bags-from-india.h1: How to export leather bags, wallets and saddlery from India
how-to-export-leather-bags-from-india.answer: To export leather bags and goods from India, register with DGFT for an IEC, take an RCMC from the Council for Leather Exports (CLE), classify each item correctly under HS 4202 (bags and wallets), 4203 (leather apparel and belts) or 4201 (saddlery), and meet the buyer's chemical and labelling rules. Buyers are mostly brands and importers who order by style after approving samples.
facts: 4202 bags and wallets, 4203 leather apparel and belts, 4201 saddlery
Chromium VI in leather touching skin: 3 mg/kg

sections.h2: What buyers abroad want and how they buy
paras: Handbags, wallets and small leather goods are sold mostly through fashion brands and private-label importers who send designs or pick from your collection, then order by style and colour after sample approval. Saddlery and harness buyers are specialist equestrian distributors who care about fit, stitching strength and hardware quality more than fashion.

Kanpur is India's main saddlery and harness centre. Kolkata, Chennai and the Delhi–Noida belt make handbags, wallets, belts and travel goods. Many factories work in both leather and non-leather materials, and that changes the HS code.

The HS code depends on the outer surface. A handbag with a leather outer is [420221](/hs-code/420221-leather-bags-wallets-and-cases-handbags); with a plastic or textile outer it is 420222; with other outers (jute, for example) 420229. Wallets carried in the pocket with a leather outer are [420231](/hs-code/420231-leather-bags-wallets-and-cases-a-kind-normally-carried-in). Suitcases are 420211 (leather) or 420212 (plastic or textile). Saddlery is [420100](/hs-code/420100-saddlery-and-harness-for-any-animal-of-any-materials). The table below shows the duty in each market for these codes.

bullets: **IEC** from DGFT: see [how to get an IEC](/guide/how-to-get-iec-code).
**RCMC from CLE** for leather goods. For canvas, jute or synthetic bags, check DGFT Appendix 2T to see which council covers your product: see [RCMC](/guide/rcmc-export-promotion-council).
**GST LUT**, AD code with your bank and an ICEGATE login.
Exotic skins (reptile and other wild species) need CITES permits and fall under Indian wildlife law. Most exporters stick to cow, buffalo, goat and sheep leather.

sections.h2: Quality, testing and compliance by market
paras: **EU and UK:** the REACH limit of 3 mg/kg chromium VI applies to leather articles that come into contact with skin, which includes bag handles, wallets and belts. REACH also restricts certain azo dyes in leather. There is no EU labelling law for bags like the one for shoes, but calling a PU bag "leather" breaks consumer law.

**US:** origin marking is required, and the FTC's guides for leather and imitation-leather products expect clear disclosure when a product only looks like leather or uses split or bonded leather. Many US buyers ask for California Proposition 65 compliance, which in practice means testing metal hardware and coated or PU parts for lead and phthalates. Since 24 July 2026 Indian bags and leather goods also pay an extra 10% US duty under Section 301, on top of the normal tariff.
**Gulf and other markets:** requirements come mainly from the buyer's specification. Agree test parameters in the purchase order.
Brands also expect social audits and often tannery ratings such as LWG. Saddlery buyers test stitching and hardware strength; ask for their test method.

bullets: Dust bag, stuffing and hang-tags as the buyer specifies; use silica gel, never DMF sachets.
Origin marking for the US, ideally sewn or embossed inside the bag.
Polybags with suffocation warnings where the buyer's market requires them.
Carton marks, carton-wise packing list and weights. Saddles are bulky, so agree carton size early because freight is charged by volume.

paras: Cost each style by leather consumption (square feet), lining, hardware, labour and overheads, then quote per piece FOB or FCA. Hardware is often bought from the buyer's nominated supplier, which affects your margin and lead time. Advance plus balance against documents, or a letter of credit, is common with new buyers; large retailers may insist on open account. Read [export pricing: FOB and CIF](/guide/export-pricing-fob-cif) and [payment terms](/guide/letter-of-credit-and-payment-terms).

bullets: Classifying a mixed-material bag by its main body when customs looks at the outer surface.
Approving a sample in one leather and producing bulk in another without re-testing.
Underestimating hardware lead times from nominated suppliers.
Mould in transit because the goods were packed before the leather dried.

steps: Get IEC, GST LUT and the CLE RCMC.
Fix HS codes for each product line with the [HS code finder](/tools/hs-code-finder).
Build a small collection with lab reports for chromium VI and azo dyes.
Meet buyers at CLE fairs and buyer-seller meets: see [how to find export buyers](/guide/how-to-find-export-buyers).
Check your readiness with the [export readiness check](/tools/export-readiness).

faqs: What HS code is a leather handbag?

A handbag with an outer surface of leather, composition leather or patent leather falls under HS 420221. If the outer surface is plastic or textile it is 420222, and other outers fall under 420229. Customs looks at the outer surface, not the lining.
Does Kanpur saddlery need a different registration?
No separate registration. Saddlery and harness under HS 420100 is a leather product, so Kanpur exporters take their RCMC from the Council for Leather Exports like other leather goods makers.
Can I export bags made of exotic leather?

Only with great care. Skins of reptiles and many wild species are controlled under CITES and under Indian wildlife law. Most Indian exporters use cow, buffalo, goat and sheep leather, which needs no CITES paperwork.
Do EU buyers require lab tests for bags?

Yes in practice. The REACH limit on chromium VI applies to leather that touches the skin, and buyers will ask for reports from an accredited lab for chromium VI and restricted azo dyes, plus any substances on their own restricted list.
sources: Federal Register: Section 301 forced-labour action and exemption annexes (28 Jul 2026)

how-to-export-spices-from-india.title: How to export spices from India: CRES, testing, MRLs
how-to-export-spices-from-india.description: Spices Board CRES registration, mandatory testing, EU pesticide and aflatoxin limits, ethylene oxide rules and US FDA steps for Indian spice exporters.
how-to-export-spices-from-india.h1: How to export spices from India
how-to-export-spices-from-india.answer: To export spices from India you need an IEC and a Certificate of Registration as Exporter of Spices (CRES) from the Spices Board, which also works as your RCMC. Each lot must meet the destination's pesticide residue, aflatoxin and ethylene oxide limits; for the EU and some other markets the Spices Board's mandatory sampling and testing applies before shipment. US buyers also need your facility registered with the FDA.
facts: CRES from Spices Board (also serves as RCMC)
Unjha (cumin), Kerala (pepper, cardamom), Guntur (chilli), Erode, Sangli, Nizamabad (turmeric)
Chilli, turmeric, ginger, nutmeg: B1 5 µg/kg, total 10 µg/kg
Food facility registration, renewed Oct–Dec of even years

sections.h2: What buyers abroad want and how they buy
paras: Most export buyers are importers, grinders and packers who buy whole spices in bulk and process them abroad, plus ethnic-food distributors who want retail packs. Bulk buyers buy on a specification: origin, grade, moisture, extraneous matter, colour or curcumin or volatile oil, and a pesticide and aflatoxin profile for their market.

Unjha is the trading centre for cumin ([090931](/hs-code/090931-cumin-and-coriander-seeds-neither-crushed-nor-ground)). Kerala supplies pepper and cardamom ([090831](/hs-code/090831-cardamom-and-nutmeg-neither-crushed-nor-ground)). Guntur dominates dried chilli ([090421](/hs-code/090421-black-pepper-and-chillies-fruits-of-the-genus-capsicum-or) whole, 090422 crushed or ground). Erode, Sangli and Nizamabad are the turmeric markets ([091030](/hs-code/091030-turmeric-ginger-and-spices)). The table below shows the duty each market charges on these codes.

bullets: **IEC** from DGFT: see [how to get an IEC](/guide/how-to-get-iec-code).

**CRES** from the Spices Board, issued under the Spices Board Act 1986. It is compulsory in addition to the IEC for exporting scheduled spices and is accepted in place of an RCMC. It runs in block periods of three years, so renew on time.
**FSSAI licence** for your processing or packing unit.

**US FDA food facility registration** for the facility that makes or packs the spice. Registrations must be renewed between 1 October and 31 December of every even-numbered year, so 2026 is a renewal year.
**Phytosanitary certificate** where the importing country asks for one, and a [certificate of origin](/guide/certificate-of-origin) to claim lower duty under a trade deal.

sections.h2: Quality, testing and compliance by market
paras: **EU and UK:** pesticide residues are controlled under Regulation (EC) 396/2005. Where no specific limit is set, a default of 0.01 mg/kg applies, which is close to zero. Aflatoxin limits for chilli, turmeric, ginger and nutmeg are 5 µg/kg for B1 and 10 µg/kg total. Ethylene oxide is not allowed as a fumigant, and its limits are set at very low levels (0.02 to 0.1 mg/kg depending on the spice in the Spices Board's table). The Spices Board runs mandatory sampling and testing of export lots to the EU for these parameters, plus Sudan dyes in chilli and turmeric powder, and certain spices need an official certificate for ethylene oxide. Since 18 December 2024 chilli and chilli powder to the UK also need an official ethylene oxide certificate.
**Singapore and Hong Kong:** since 6 May 2024 the Spices Board has required every spice consignment to these two destinations to carry its cleared ethylene oxide test report.

**US:** there is no FDA pre-approval, but the facility must be registered, the US importer files prior notice and verifies suppliers, and FDA tests at the border. Salmonella and pesticide residues without a US tolerance are the usual reasons for detention. Whole and ground spices under HTS headings 0904 to 0910 (pepper, chilli, cardamom, cumin, coriander, turmeric, ginger and others) are on the exemption list (Annex II, Part A) of the 10% Section 301 duty the US has charged on most Indian goods since 24 July 2026. Blends, sauces and extracts classified under other headings may not be exempt, so check the code.
**Gulf:** buyers check pesticide residues, labelling and shelf life. Get the buyer's specification and test against it.

bullets: Food-grade bags with liners for bulk; moisture control matters because damp stock grows mould and aflatoxin.
Use steam sterilisation where the buyer wants a low microbial count. Do not fumigate with ethylene oxide.
Lot numbers on every bag, matching the test report and the shipping documents.
Retail packs need the destination's labelling (ingredients, net weight, importer address, allergens, language).

paras: Spices are traded per tonne, usually FOB or CFR in US dollars, and prices move with the domestic crop and auction markets, so keep offers short-dated. Contracts should state who pays for testing and what happens if a lot fails at destination. Advance or cash against documents is common with smaller buyers; letters of credit are used for larger lots. See [export pricing](/guide/export-pricing-fob-cif) and the [price calculator](/tools/export-price-calculator).

bullets: Buying from the open market without residue history, then failing EU tests after paying the farmer or trader.
Testing one composite sample when the shipment mixes several lots.
Letting the FDA registration lapse in a renewal year, which stops US shipments.
Fumigating with chemicals the destination does not allow.

steps: Get your IEC, FSSAI licence and CRES from the Spices Board.
Choose one or two spices and markets; check duty in the table below and the [import duty tool](/tools/import-duty).
Line up an NABL-accredited lab and supply from farmer groups or traders who can show residue history.
Register the facility with the US FDA if you will sell to the US.
Find buyers: see [how to find export buyers](/guide/how-to-find-export-buyers).

faqs: Is Spices Board registration compulsory?

Yes. The Spices Board says a Certificate of Registration as Exporter of Spices (CRES) is mandatory in addition to the IEC for exporting spices. The CRES is also accepted in place of an RCMC, so you do not need a separate council membership for spices.
What is the EU aflatoxin limit for chilli and turmeric?

5 µg/kg for aflatoxin B1 and 10 µg/kg for total aflatoxins. The same limits apply to ginger and nutmeg. The Spices Board tests export lots to the EU against these limits under its mandatory sampling and testing programme.
Why is ethylene oxide a problem for spice exports?

Ethylene oxide was used to kill microbes in spices, but the EU does not allow it, and limits are set at very low levels. Since May 2024 the Spices Board has also required ethylene oxide testing for every spice consignment to Singapore and Hong Kong. Use steam sterilisation instead.
Do Indian spices pay the 10% US Section 301 duty?

No, for spices classified under HTS headings 0904 to 0910. The US notice that added 10% to most Indian goods from 24 July 2026 lists these headings in its exemption list (Annex II, Part A). Spice blends, sauces or extracts under other headings may not be covered, so check the exact US code with your importer's broker.
Does my spice unit need FDA approval to sell to the US?

FDA does not approve facilities in advance, but the facility must be registered with the FDA and the registration renewed between 1 October and 31 December of each even-numbered year. FDA can detain shipments at the border for Salmonella or residues.
Can I export cumin to Europe without testing?

Not safely. EU pesticide limits apply to cumin, and the default limit for pesticides without a specific limit is 0.01 mg/kg. Test each lot before shipment and keep the report with the lot number on your documents.
sources: Spices Board: mandatory sampling and testing circular
US FDA: biennial food facility registration renewal
Spices Board: ethylene oxide testing for Singapore and Hong Kong (Circular 01/2024-25)
Spices Board: ethylene oxide test for chilli to the UK (Circular 20/2024-25)
Federal Register: Section 301 forced-labour action and exemption annexes (28 Jul 2026)

how-to-export-rice-from-india.title: How to export rice from India: APEDA, RCAC and rules
how-to-export-rice-from-india.description: Basmati and non-basmati rice export: APEDA RCMC, contract registration (RCAC), current DGFT conditions, EIC inspection for Europe and EU residue limits.
how-to-export-rice-from-india.h1: How to export rice from India
how-to-export-rice-from-india.answer: To export rice from India you need an IEC and an RCMC from APEDA, and every export contract must be registered with APEDA to get a Registration-cum-Allocation Certificate (RCAC) before shipment. This has long applied to basmati and, since DGFT Notification 33/2025-26 of 24 September 2025, also applies to non-basmati and broken rice. Shipments to the EU, UK, Norway, Iceland, Liechtenstein and Switzerland also need an EIC inspection certificate.
facts: RCAC, valid for shipment within 45 days
Basmati: Haryana, Punjab (Karnal, Amritsar); non-basmati: AP, Chhattisgarh, West Bengal

sections.h2: What buyers abroad want and how they buy
paras: Basmati buyers are importers, packers and distributors who buy by variety (for example 1121 or traditional basmati), type (raw, steam, sella or golden sella), average grain length, broken percentage, moisture and age. Many want rice packed under their own brand. Non-basmati buyers, including government tenders and large traders, buy on broken percentage, variety and price, often in bulk or 25–50 kg bags.
Milled rice is HS [100630](/hs-code/100630-rice-semi-milled-or-wholly-milled) and broken rice is [100640](/hs-code/100640-rice-broken). The table below shows duty in the main markets.

sections.h2: Export policy and registrations as of November 2026
bullets: **IEC** from DGFT and **RCMC from APEDA**, which DGFT lists as the body for cereals.

**Contract registration (RCAC):** upload the LC, contract or proforma invoice on the APEDA site and get an RCAC before shipment. Customs asks for it. The RCAC is valid for shipment within 45 days of issue. For non-basmati the fee is ₹8 per tonne plus GST, minimum ₹50 (APEDA trade notice, 25 September 2025); for basmati it is ₹70 per tonne plus GST (APEDA trade notice, 1 October 2025).

**Basmati conditions:** grains must be longer than 6.61 mm with a length-to-breadth ratio above 3.5, and basmati may not be exported on documents-against-acceptance (D/A) terms unless a bank guarantee or ECGC cover backs the sale.
**Broken rice:** DGFT moved it from Prohibited to Free on 7 March 2025 (Notification 61/2024-25). It is covered by the September 2025 contract-registration condition.

**Europe:** under DGFT Notification 07/2026-27 of 10 April 2026, rice to EU member states, the UK, Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway and Switzerland needs a Certificate of Inspection from EIC or EIA, which you upload with the RCAC application. The six-month exemption for other European countries ran until 1 October 2026, and DGFT had not published an extension by 30 October 2026, so check with EIC or APEDA before shipping rice anywhere in Europe.

**US and China:** only from mills registered with the Directorate of Plant Protection, Quarantine and Storage. **Saudi Arabia:** only from establishments with ISO 22000 or HACCP; merchant exporters must show a certificate from the SFDA-accredited mill.
**Indonesia, Russia and Iran** need pre-shipment testing or inspection by approved labs, as listed in the APEDA trade notice.
paras: Rice policy has changed often since 2022, so check the DGFT notifications page before each new contract.

sections.h2: Quality, testing and compliance by market
paras: **EU and UK:** pesticide limits are strict. The EU limit for the fungicide tricyclazole in rice is 0.01 mg/kg, and basmati shipments have been rejected for residues. Work with farmers on spray schedules, and test every lot at an accredited lab.

**US:** besides mill registration with plant quarantine, the US importer must meet FDA food rules and your facility must be registered with the FDA. Pesticide residues without a US tolerance make the rice violative. Since 24 July 2026 Indian rice also pays an extra 10% US duty under Section 301; rice is not on the notice's exemption list.
**Gulf:** basmati buyers want consistent grain length, cooking quality and aged rice. Saudi Arabia's food-safety system requirement is in the APEDA notice above.

bullets: Retail packs (1, 5, 10 kg) in the buyer's brand, bulk in 25 or 50 kg PP or jute bags with liners.
Fumigation and a phytosanitary certificate where required by the destination.
Label language, net weight, crop year and importer details as the destination requires; check private-label artwork before printing.
Keep moisture under the contract limit; condensation in containers damages rice.

paras: Rice is quoted per tonne in US dollars, FOB Kandla, Mundra, Kakinada or other ports, or CIF. Prices track paddy prices and global competition, so validity is short. Letters of credit and cash against documents are both common; insure unsecured terms with [ECGC](/guide/ecgc-export-credit-insurance). Basmati cannot be sold on D/A terms without a bank guarantee or ECGC cover. Remember that the LC or contract you upload for the RCAC must match the shipment.

bullets: Shipping without a valid RCAC or after it expires.
Mixing lots with different residue profiles in one container.
Forgetting the EIC certificate for Europe.
Quoting long-validity prices in a market that moves weekly.

steps: Get IEC and APEDA RCMC: see [RCMC](/guide/rcmc-export-promotion-council).
Check market duty in the table below and the [import duty tool](/tools/import-duty).
Line up a mill with the registrations your market needs (plant quarantine, ISO 22000 or HACCP).
Sign the contract, register it with APEDA, then book freight: see [shipping and customs](/guide/export-shipping-and-customs-clearance).

faqs: Is non-basmati rice export allowed now?

Yes. As of DGFT Notification 33/2025-26 of 24 September 2025, non-basmati rice, including broken rice, can be exported only after the contract is registered with APEDA and an RCAC is issued. Check DGFT notifications before each contract because rice policy changes often.
What is an RCAC?

A Registration-cum-Allocation Certificate issued by APEDA after you upload your LC, contract or proforma invoice. Customs needs it with the export documents. For non-basmati rice it is valid for shipment within 45 days of issue.
Do I need an inspection certificate for rice to Europe?

Yes for the EU, the UK, Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway and Switzerland. DGFT Notification 07/2026-27 of 10 April 2026 requires a Certificate of Inspection from EIC or EIA, which you upload when applying for the RCAC. Other European countries were exempt until 1 October 2026 and no extension had been published by 30 October 2026, so check before shipping.
Can a merchant exporter sell rice to Saudi Arabia?
Yes, but the rice must come from a mill with ISO 22000 or HACCP, and before the RCAC is issued you must upload a certificate from the SFDA-accredited establishment you bought from.

APEDA: trade notice on basmati contract registration (1 Oct 2025)
DGFT: Notification 33/2025-26 on non-basmati rice (24 Sep 2025)
DGFT: Notification 07/2026-27 on EIC inspection for Europe (10 Apr 2026)
Federal Register: Section 301 forced-labour action and exemption annexes (28 Jul 2026)

how-to-export-garments-from-india.title: How to export garments from India: AEPC, audits, labels
how-to-export-garments-from-india.description: Readymade garment exports: AEPC registration, buyer audits, EU, UK and US labelling and chemical rules, children's wear testing, sizing and payment terms.
how-to-export-garments-from-india.h1: How to export garments from India
how-to-export-garments-from-india.answer: To export garments from India you need an IEC, an RCMC from the Apparel Export Promotion Council (AEPC), correct HS codes (chapter 61 for knits, 62 for wovens) and a factory that passes the buyer's social and chemical compliance. Labels must show fibre content, care and origin in the format each market requires. Most orders come through brands, retailers and buying houses.
facts: FTC Textile Act and Care Labeling Rule

sections.h2: What buyers abroad want and how they buy
paras: Brands and retailers buy through their own sourcing offices or buying houses in India. They send a tech pack, then approve lab dips, fit samples, a pre-production sample and size set before bulk, and inspect the goods before shipment, usually on an AQL sampling plan.

Tiruppur is the knitwear centre (T-shirts [610910](/hs-code/610910-t-shirts-cotton-knitted-or-crocheted), polo shirts 610510, babywear [611120](/hs-code/611120-babies-garments-cotton)). Ludhiana makes sweaters (611020) and winterwear. Noida, Gurugram, Bengaluru and Jaipur make woven shirts ([620520](/hs-code/620520-men-s-shirts-boys-of-cotton)), dresses (620442) and blouses (620630). The HS code changes with knit or woven, fibre and gender, and the table below shows duty for each code in each market.

bullets: **IEC**, **GST LUT** and **RCMC from AEPC**: see [RCMC](/guide/rcmc-export-promotion-council).
**Social audits** that buyers commonly accept: amfori BSCI, Sedex SMETA and WRAP. Ask the buyer which one before booking.
**Environmental and chemical programmes** for dyeing and washing units, such as ZDHC wastewater and chemical lists, are often required by large brands.
Claim [RoDTEP and duty drawback](/guide/rodtep-and-duty-drawback) on every shipping bill.

paras: **EU:** fibre content must be labelled using the fibre names in Regulation (EU) 1007/2011, with percentages by weight in descending order. REACH restricts azo dyes that release listed amines above 30 mg/kg in textiles that touch the skin, along with other substances. Since 13 December 2024 the General Product Safety Regulation requires an EU-based responsible operator and traceability details for consumer products; your buyer handles this, but they will ask for batch information on labels.
**UK:** the Textile Products (Labelling and Fibre Names) Regulations 2012 apply, and UK REACH carries the same azo restriction.

**US:** the FTC Textile Act requires fibre content, country of origin and the identity of the maker or seller (often an RN number), and the Care Labeling Rule requires permanent care instructions. All clothing textiles must meet the general flammability standard. Children's garments, including babywear, need third-party testing at a CPSC-accepted lab, a Children's Product Certificate from the importer and tracking labels. Since 8 July 2026 importers must e-file certificate data with US Customs at entry, so they will ask for your test reports before shipment. Since 24 July 2026 Indian garments also pay an extra 10% US duty under Section 301, on top of the normal tariff.
**Gulf and others:** requirements come mostly from the buyer's labelling and test manual. Get it before you print labels.

bullets: Use the buyer's size chart and grading rules; US, UK and EU sizes do not convert one-to-one.
Main label, size label, fibre and care label (permanent, sewn in), origin "Made in India", and price or barcode tickets as the buyer specifies.
Polybags with warnings where required, carton marks and an assortment (ratio) packing list.
Check trims (zips, snaps, prints) for the chemical limits in the buyer's restricted substances list.

paras: Garments are quoted per piece, FOB, built from fabric consumption, trims, CMT, washing, testing, overhead and margin. Large brands mostly pay on open account 30 to 90 days after shipment, so credit insurance through [ECGC](/guide/ecgc-export-credit-insurance) matters. Smaller importers often pay an advance with the balance against documents. Use the [export price calculator](/tools/export-price-calculator).

bullets: Using fibre names the EU list does not allow (brand names instead of the legal name).
Skipping CPSIA testing for babywear headed to the US.
Shrinkage and colour fastness failures discovered at final inspection.
Accepting audit-heavy buyers before the factory's documents, wages and fire safety are in order.

steps: Get IEC, GST LUT and AEPC RCMC.
Fix HS codes with the [HS code finder](/tools/hs-code-finder) and compare duty using the table below.
Get a recognised social audit done and keep test reports for your main fabrics.
Meet buyers through AEPC fairs and buying houses: see [how to find export buyers](/guide/how-to-find-export-buyers).

faqs: Which export council handles readymade garments?
The Apparel Export Promotion Council (AEPC). DGFT lists readymade garments under AEPC, so you take your RCMC from it to claim export benefits and join AEPC fairs.
What must a garment label show for the EU?

Fibre composition with the legal fibre names from Regulation (EU) 1007/2011 and percentages by weight. Care symbols and origin are not set by that regulation but buyers almost always require them, and some member states have their own language rules.
Do babywear exports to the US need special testing?

Yes. Children's products need third-party testing at a CPSC-accepted laboratory for applicable rules such as lead and, where relevant, phthalates, plus tracking labels and a Children's Product Certificate issued by the US importer or manufacturer.
Is a BSCI or SEDEX audit a legal requirement?
No. They are buyer requirements. But most brands and retailers will not place orders without a recognised social audit, so treat it as a condition of doing business with them.

US FTC: labelling under the Textile and Wool Acts

how-to-export-home-textiles-from-india.title: How to export home textiles and carpets from India
how-to-export-home-textiles-from-india.description: Bed linen, towels, furnishings and carpets: which council to join, OEKO-TEX and child-labour expectations, EU and US labelling, packing and payment.
how-to-export-home-textiles-from-india.h1: How to export home textiles and carpets from India
how-to-export-home-textiles-from-india.answer: To export home textiles from India you need an IEC and an RCMC from the right council: TEXPROCIL for cotton made-ups such as bed linen and towels, HEPC for handloom products, PDEXCIL for powerloom products, and the Carpet Export Promotion Council for handmade carpets. Buyers expect fibre labelling, chemical test reports such as OEKO-TEX, and, for carpets, proof that no child labour was used.
facts: TEXPROCIL, HEPC, PDEXCIL, Carpet EPC (by product and process)
Flammability standards for carpets and rugs (CPSC)

sections.h2: What buyers abroad want and how they buy
paras: Home textiles are bought by retail chains, department stores, online sellers and importers who supply hotels. They order by programme (a range in several colours and sizes) and repeat if sell-through is good. Specifications cover GSM or thread count, dimensions with tolerances, shrinkage, colour fastness and packing.

Panipat makes durries, bath mats, blankets, throws and cushion covers, much of it from recycled yarn. Karur weaves table, kitchen and bed linen. Solapur is known for terry towels and chaddars. Bhadohi and Mirzapur make hand-knotted and hand-tufted carpets. Jaipur makes block-printed bedding, quilts and rugs.

Typical codes: cotton bed linen [630231](/hs-code/630231-bed-linen-and-towels-cotton), terry towels [630260](/hs-code/630260-bed-linen-and-towels-terry-towelling-or-similar-terry), furnishings 630492 and 630419, other made-ups 630790, hand-knotted carpets [570110](/hs-code/570110-hand-knotted-carpets-knotted), woven carpets 570231 and tufted carpets [570390](/hs-code/570390-tufted-carpets). The table below gives duty for each.

bullets: **TEXPROCIL:** cotton made-ups including bed linen, terry towels, curtains, table and kitchen linen (DGFT Appendix 2T).
**HEPC:** all handloom products, including home furnishings, carpets and floor coverings.
**PDEXCIL:** powerloom products.
**Carpet Export Promotion Council (CEPC):** handmade, hand-knotted and hand-tufted carpets, rugs, durries, kelims and namdas.
Plus **IEC**, **GST LUT** and bank AD code: see [RCMC](/guide/rcmc-export-promotion-council) for how to apply.

paras: **EU and UK:** textile products, including bed linen and towels, need fibre content labels using the legal fibre names (Regulation (EU) 1007/2011; in the UK, the 2012 labelling regulations). REACH restricts azo dyes in textiles that touch the skin. Many buyers ask for OEKO-TEX Standard 100 certificates and, for organic claims, GOTS; these are private schemes, not laws.

**US:** the FTC Textile Act covers household textiles (fibre content, origin, maker identity), and carpets and rugs must meet CPSC flammability standards. US law (Section 307 of the Tariff Act) bars goods made with forced or indentured child labour, and CBP can detain them. The US Labor Department's list of goods produced with child or forced labour includes carpets from India. Since 24 July 2026 Indian home textiles and carpets also pay an extra 10% US duty under Section 301, on top of the normal tariff.

**Carpets and child labour:** buyers in the EU and US commonly ask for certification such as GoodWeave, plus records of weavers and sub-contractors. The EU Forced Labour Regulation (EU) 2024/3015 will apply from 14 December 2027.
**Gulf:** buyers focus on specification and price; agree labels and tests in the order.

bullets: Retail packs with insert cards, size and fibre labels, care instructions and barcodes as the buyer specifies.
Towels and linen sold by weight or GSM need weight tolerances agreed in the contract.
Carpets rolled with polythene and hessian or boxed, with the size and knot or tuft details on the label.
Wool carpets need moth protection that the destination allows; check the buyer's restricted substances list.

paras: Made-ups are quoted per piece or set, carpets per square foot or square metre, usually FOB. Cotton yarn prices move, so state a validity date. Large retailers work on open account; smaller importers pay an advance with balance against documents. See [payment terms](/guide/letter-of-credit-and-payment-terms) and [ECGC cover](/guide/ecgc-export-credit-insurance).

bullets: Joining the wrong council, which delays your RCMC and incentive claims.
Shipping towels that miss GSM or size tolerance.
Unmapped sub-contracted weaving that cannot prove it is free of child labour.
Calling a blend "100% cotton" or using non-legal fibre names on EU labels.

steps: Decide your product and process, then register with the matching council.
Confirm HS codes with the [HS code finder](/tools/hs-code-finder) and check duty in the table below.
Get OEKO-TEX or the tests your target buyers ask for; for carpets, map your weaving network.
Find buyers at council fairs: see [how to find export buyers](/guide/how-to-find-export-buyers).

faqs: Which council should a Panipat home textile exporter join?

It depends on the product and how it is made. Cotton made-ups go to TEXPROCIL, handloom products to HEPC, powerloom products to PDEXCIL, and handmade carpets to the Carpet Export Promotion Council, as listed in DGFT Appendix 2T.
Is OEKO-TEX certification compulsory?

No. OEKO-TEX Standard 100 is a private certification. The legal rules are chemical restrictions like REACH, but many European buyers use OEKO-TEX as their proof, so it often decides whether you get the order.
Why do carpet buyers ask for child-labour certification?

US law bars goods made with forced or indentured child labour, the US Labor Department lists Indian carpets among goods at risk, and the EU Forced Labour Regulation applies from 14 December 2027. Certification such as GoodWeave and weaver records help buyers show due diligence.
Do carpets need fire testing for the US?
Yes. Carpets and rugs sold in the US must meet CPSC flammability standards. Your buyer will usually ask for a test report from an accredited lab for each construction.

how-to-export-brass-and-handicrafts-from.title: How to export brass, metal and wood handicrafts from India
how-to-export-brass-and-handicrafts-from.description: Brass artware, steel kitchenware and wooden furniture: EPCH registration, lead and food-contact rules, EUDR dates for wood, packing and payment terms.
how-to-export-brass-and-handicrafts-from.h1: How to export brass, metal ware and wooden handicrafts from India
how-to-export-brass-and-handicrafts-from.answer: To export brass, metal ware and wooden handicrafts from India you need an IEC and an RCMC from the Export Promotion Council for Handicrafts (EPCH). Then meet the buyer's rules on lead in coatings, food-contact safety for kitchenware and timber legality for wood. For wooden furniture sold into the EU, the Deforestation Regulation applies from 30 December 2026 for most importers. Breakage-proof packing decides your claims.
facts: 30 Dec 2026 (large, medium, and small firms already under EUTR); 30 Jun 2027 (other micro, small)
Max 90 ppm on furniture and children's items

sections.h2: What buyers abroad want and how they buy
paras: Handicraft buyers are importers, home-décor chains, department stores and online sellers. Many first meet suppliers at EPCH's IHGF Delhi Fair, then order from a catalogue or develop designs with you. Orders are by item and finish, often with a mixed container across many items.

Moradabad makes brass and other metal artware, lamps and tableware ([741980](/hs-code/741980-brass-and-copper-articles-thereof-in-chapter-74) for copper-alloy articles) and steel kitchenware ([732393](/hs-code/732393-steel-kitchenware-table)). Saharanpur is known for carved wood, Jodhpur for wooden furniture ([940360](/hs-code/940360-furniture-wooden-other-than-for-office)), and Aligarh for locks and hardware. The table below shows duty for these codes.

bullets: **IEC**, **GST LUT** and **RCMC from EPCH**, which DGFT lists for art metal ware, wood ware and other handicrafts: see [RCMC](/guide/rcmc-export-promotion-council).
If you make industrial stainless steel kitchenware rather than handicrafts, check DGFT Appendix 2T to confirm whether your product sits with EPCH or EEPC India.
Keep timber purchase records and transit passes for every wooden order; buyers need them for legality checks.

sections.h2: Quality, testing and compliance by market
paras: **Lead and coatings:** in the US, paint and similar coatings with more than 90 ppm lead are banned on furniture and on toys and children's articles. Many US buyers also ask for California Proposition 65 compliance, which matters for brass because brass alloys often contain lead. In the EU, REACH limits lead in articles that children can put in their mouths. Ask your lacquer and paint suppliers for test reports.

**Food contact:** kitchenware sold in the EU must meet Regulation (EC) 1935/2004, which says materials must not transfer substances into food that endanger health. German buyers commonly ask for LFGB migration tests. Unlined brass and copper should not touch acidic food, so tableware is usually tin-lined, stainless-lined or sold as decorative only.

**Wood:** the EU Deforestation Regulation (EUDR) covers wood and wooden furniture. According to the European Commission, it applies from 30 December 2026 for large and medium operators, and for micro and small operators already covered by the EU Timber Regulation (which included wooden furniture); other micro and small operators follow on 30 June 2027. Your EU buyer will ask for the geolocation of the forest or plantation and proof of legal harvest. FSC certification helps but does not replace this. The US Lacey Act also makes importing illegally harvested wood an offence. Sheesham (Dalbergia sissoo) is still listed under CITES. Since a 2022 change, items in which the sheesham wood weighs under 10 kg each can ship without CITES permits; heavier pieces such as beds and dining tables still need them. Confirm the current rule with EPCH before quoting.
**Wooden packaging** must be ISPM-15 treated and marked for most destinations.

bullets: Pack to the buyer's drop and vibration test standard; e-commerce buyers often require ISTA testing.
Use moulded pulp, corner protectors and double-wall cartons; wrap polished brass in acid-free paper so it does not tarnish.
Kiln-dry wood to the moisture level the buyer specifies and use desiccants to stop mould and cracking in the container.
Label each carton with item code, quantity and "Made in India"; the US requires origin marking on the article itself where possible.

paras: Quote per piece FOB, with metal, wood and finish costed separately, and state the minimum per item and per container. Samples are usually charged. Smaller importers often pay an advance with the balance against documents; large chains may want open account. Use the [export price calculator](/tools/export-price-calculator) and read [Incoterms](/guide/incoterms-for-indian-exporters).

For the US, most Indian goods have paid an extra 10% duty under Section 301 since 24 July 2026. Steel, copper and wood products that already pay US Section 232 tariffs are excluded from it but pay those instead, so ask the importer's customs broker which applies to each item before quoting.

bullets: Lacquers or paints bought on price with no lead test report.
Selling decorative brass as food-safe tableware.
No timber legality paperwork when an EU buyer asks for EUDR data.
Packing that passes in the factory but fails a drop test, leading to breakage claims.

steps: Get IEC, GST LUT and EPCH RCMC.
Fix HS codes with the [HS code finder](/tools/hs-code-finder) and compare duty in the table below.
Get lead and food-contact tests for your main finishes and organise timber records.
Exhibit or visit EPCH fairs and contact buyers: see [how to find export buyers](/guide/how-to-find-export-buyers).

faqs: Which council should a Moradabad brass exporter join?

The Export Promotion Council for Handicrafts (EPCH). DGFT's list of councils assigns art metal ware, wood ware and other handicrafts to EPCH, and it runs the IHGF Delhi Fair where many buyers first meet suppliers.
When does the EU Deforestation Regulation apply to wooden furniture?

The European Commission states it applies from 30 December 2026 for large and medium operators and for micro and small operators already covered by the EU Timber Regulation, and from 30 June 2027 for other micro and small operators. Wooden furniture is covered, so EU buyers will ask for plot geolocation and legality proof.
Can I sell brass utensils as food-safe?

Only if they are lined or tested for the market. The EU requires food-contact materials not to transfer harmful substances into food, and buyers ask for migration tests. Unlined brass and copper are usually sold as decorative.
What lead limit applies to painted furniture in the US?
US rules ban paint and similar surface coatings containing more than 90 ppm lead on furniture for consumer use and on toys and children's articles. Get test reports for each paint or lacquer you use.

how-to-export-shrimp-from-india.title: How to export shrimp from India: MPEDA, EIC, US duties
how-to-export-shrimp-from-india.description: Frozen shrimp and seafood export: MPEDA registration, EIC plant approval for the EU, antibiotic rules, US anti-dumping and Section 301 duties and DS-2031.
how-to-export-shrimp-from-india.h1: How to export shrimp and frozen seafood from India
how-to-export-shrimp-from-india.answer: To export shrimp from India you need an IEC, registration as an exporter with MPEDA, and a processing plant approved by the Export Inspection Council (EIC) for markets such as the EU, which issues the health certificate. Every lot must be free of banned antibiotics. In the US, Indian shrimp faces anti-dumping and countervailing duties plus, since 24 July 2026, a 10% Section 301 duty, and only farmed shrimp can enter.
facts: Anti-dumping order since 2005; countervailing order since Dec 2024
Only farmed shrimp from India eligible; DS-2031 with every shipment

sections.h2: What buyers abroad want and how they buy
paras: Most Indian shrimp is farmed vannamei from Andhra Pradesh, processed into frozen headless shell-on, peeled, deveined or cooked forms. Buyers are importers, retail chains and food-service distributors who buy by count per pound or kilo, glaze percentage, net weight and processing style, and who audit the plant.

Frozen shrimp is HS [030617](/hs-code/030617-shrimp-and-prawns-frozen); Kochi and Gujarat exporters also ship cuttlefish and squid (030743), frozen fish (030389) and fish meat (030499). The table below shows the normal duty in each market and what trade deals change; US trade-remedy duties are explained here instead.

bullets: **IEC** from DGFT and **registration as an exporter with MPEDA**, which DGFT lists as the body for marine products and which serves as your RCMC.

**EIC approval of the processing plant** for the EU and other markets that require it. Approved Indian plants appear on the EU's list of establishments; you cannot ship to the EU from an unlisted plant.
**Export health certificate** issued by EIC's agencies for each consignment where the importing country requires it.
**US FDA food facility registration** for the plant, renewed between 1 October and 31 December of even years, and a seafood HACCP plan.
**China** requires the overseas manufacturer to be registered with its customs authority before export.

paras: **EU:** residues of banned antibiotics such as nitrofurans and chloramphenicol lead to border rejections. From 3 September 2026 the EU also requires that farmed animals, including aquaculture shrimp, were not given antimicrobials for growth promotion or antimicrobials reserved for human use; the exporting country must be on the EU's commodity-specific list and the health certificate carries this attestation. Confirm with EIC that your product is covered before contracting.

**US:** importers must verify that the foreign processor follows FDA's seafood HACCP rules, and FDA can detain shipments found with unapproved drugs. Shrimp is also covered by NOAA's Seafood Import Monitoring Program, under which the US importer reports harvest data for each shipment, so keep pond and harvest records for every lot. Use only hatcheries and farms with residue testing records.
**Everywhere:** test raw material before processing; EIC runs India's residue monitoring for aquaculture, but buyers expect your own lot testing too.

sections.h2: US duties and Section 609, as verified on 3 November 2026
bullets: **Anti-dumping duty:** an order on frozen warmwater shrimp from India has been in place since 2005. Rates are company-specific and reset in annual reviews; the latest final results (for February 2024 to January 2025) were published on 4 September 2026.
**Countervailing duty:** an order on Indian shrimp was issued in December 2024. Rates are also company-specific.

**Section 301:** under USTR's notice of 23 July 2026 (Federal Register, 28 July 2026), products of India entered on or after 24 July 2026 pay an additional 10% on top of the normal duty, except goods on the notice's exemption list (Annex II, Part A). Frozen shrimp (HTS 0306.17) is not on that list, so the 10% applies, and anti-dumping and countervailing duties continue on top. A separate Section 301 investigation on excess capacity, which includes India, had no announced action when we checked.
**Section 609 (sea turtles):** India is not certified, so only shrimp from aquaculture can enter the US. Every shipment must carry the DS-2031 declaration.
The US importer pays these duties at entry, so they come straight out of your price. Agree who bears later rate changes in the contract.
Declare net weight after glaze; over-glazing is treated as short weight.
Carton labels with species name, count, net weight, plant approval number, production date, lot and "Product of India".
Cold chain at -18°C or colder, with temperature logs from plant to port.

sections.h2: Pricing, payment, common mistakes and how to start
paras: Shrimp is quoted per kg or per pound by count, usually CFR or CIF. Letters of credit and documents against payment are common; open account with large US importers carries risk, so use [ECGC](/guide/ecgc-export-credit-insurance). Common mistakes: shipping from a plant not on the EU list, missing DS-2031 forms, buying farm shrimp without residue records, and quoting US prices without allowing for anti-dumping, countervailing and Section 301 duties.
steps: Get IEC and MPEDA registration; apply to EIC for plant approval.
Register the plant with the US FDA and build a seafood HACCP plan if you will sell to the US.
Check market duty in the table below and the [import duty tool](/tools/import-duty).
Find buyers: see [how to find export buyers](/guide/how-to-find-export-buyers).

faqs: Is MPEDA registration compulsory for shrimp exporters?
Yes. Exporters of marine products must register with MPEDA, which DGFT lists as the body for marine products. The registration also serves as the RCMC you need for export benefits.
Can Indian wild-caught shrimp be exported to the US?
No. India is not certified under Section 609 of US law on sea-turtle protection, so only farmed shrimp is eligible. Every shrimp shipment, farmed or wild, must carry the DS-2031 declaration.
What extra US duties apply to Indian shrimp?

As verified on 3 November 2026: company-specific anti-dumping and countervailing duties, plus a 10% Section 301 duty on Indian goods entered from 24 July 2026. Check USTR and Federal Register notices before quoting, as these change.
Do I need EIC approval to export shrimp to the EU?

Yes. The processing plant must be approved by EIC and appear on the EU list of approved establishments, and each consignment needs a health certificate. From 3 September 2026 the certificate also carries the EU antimicrobial-use attestation.
Do EU rules on antibiotics affect farmers or only processors?
Both. The EU rules from 3 September 2026 cover how the shrimp was raised, so processors need records from hatcheries and farms showing no growth-promoting or reserved antimicrobials were used.
